post.description: Leave an account you are a member of. Ends YOUR OWN membership only — the route takes no target, so it cannot be used on anyone else. AUTHORIZATION: no global permission is required, deliberately. Unlike the other member routes this does NOT require account::members::manage: revoking that capability turns self-service management off, and must not also trap existing members inside an account they want to leave. Authority is your own membership in THIS account, resolved per request — a non-member gets 404, identical to a nonexistent account id, and a personal account gets 422. Refuses (422 `LAST_OWNER`) if you are the account's sole owner: an account must keep at least one owner, so promote another member to `owner` first (see PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/members/{user_id}). Leaving also cancels every still-pending project transfer you are a party to on this account's projects, in the same transaction. Leaving does NOT delete or reassign the projects and datasets you created in the account — they stay with the account. FRONTEND NOTE (#149): do NOT gate a Leave affordance on `Account.membersManageContext` succeeding. That preflight requires account::members::manage AND the `admin` floor, so in the exact deployment where this route matters — self-service management switched off — it returns 403 while Leave is still available. Gate Leave on being a member, not on the management preflight; and note that a sole owner will get 422 `LAST_OWNER` here, which is a prompt to transfer ownership first, not an error to hide.

get.description: The account's membership audit ledger: who joined, left, was removed or was re-roled, when, and who did it. Paged, newest first. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account — a non-member gets 404 (never 403), identical to a nonexistent account id; a bare `member` gets 403. THE LEDGER RECORDS COMPLETED MUTATIONS, NOT ATTEMPTS. Each row is written inside the same database transaction as the mutation it records, so a refused action (an escalation refused as ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR, a removal refused as LAST_OWNER) leaves NO row at all. Read this as `what happened to this account`, never as `who tried what`. The rows are append-only and permanent — a correction is a new row, never an edit — and they are deleted only when the account itself is. This projection omits the unattended `system` provisioning event that seeds a new account, and on platform staff actions it reports `actor_kind: admin` WITHOUT the individual staff member's id: you learn that platform staff acted, not which employee. It does NOT omit every `system` event: a membership that ended with no attributable human actor — for example because the user account itself was deleted — is a real event in this account and IS shown, as `actor_kind: system`.

post.description: Invite an email address to an account you administer. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account; a non-member gets 404 (never 403), identical to a nonexistent account id. ENUMERATION SAFETY — THIS IS A CONTRACT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. This endpoint returns 202 with the body {"status":"sent"} and nothing else, IDENTICALLY, in all four cases: the address belongs to no user; it belongs to a user; it belongs to a user who is ALREADY A MEMBER of this account; a live invitation for it already exists (idempotent — the existing token stands). The last two are server-side no-ops. Do not add a distinguishing status or code for them: `409 ALREADY_A_MEMBER` would tell the caller both that the address is registered and that it is in this account, which is exactly the account-enumeration oracle invitations exist to avoid. THE INVITE LINK IS NOT IN THIS RESPONSE, deliberately — returning it only when a new invitation was created would itself be the oracle. The token is stored only as a SHA-256, so it cannot be re-derived later either: list the account's pending invitations with GET /accounts/{account_id}/invitations and mint a link with POST /accounts/{account_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/resend. Put that token in the FRAGMENT of your invite URL (`/invite#<token>`), never in a path or query — a token in a URL leaks through Referer headers, browser history, proxy access logs and screen shares. ROLE CEILING: the role you request must be at or below your own role in this account — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise, and no invitation is written. An admin may invite an `admin` or a `member`, but may not invite an `owner`. Accepting this invitation creates an account membership at the stated role. The role is FROZEN at issue — it is exactly what the invitee will receive, and it is never silently re-interpreted. Revoking the invitation before it is accepted withdraws the offer; it cannot withdraw a membership already created (remove the member instead). NOTE the redemption endpoint is NOT part of this release: until it ships, an invitation can be created, listed, resent and revoked, but not accepted. Account membership is an implicit grant: a `member` holds at least Viewer on EVERY project, dataset and artifact in the account, an `admin` holds Editor on all of them, and an `owner` holds Owner — including delete, transfer and share — on projects they did not create. Adding, removing or re-roling a member changes all of that in one call.

Distinguish by the error CODE. NOTE none of these depends on the email address you supplied

`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — **the same three bytes in
 every case**.

That last rule is deliberate and is broader than it looks: the address is stored verbatim and will one day be placed in a mail header (so control characters must never reach the table), and an invisible character would make a second, distinct invitation for what a human reads as one address. It also means INTERNATIONALIZED addresses (SMTPUTF8 local parts, IDN domains) are refused; there is no mail transport in this product yet, and the right way to support them later is to normalize to the ASCII form at the boundary

post.description: Mint a FRESH token for a pending invitation and return it, pushing out the expiry. This is how you obtain an invite link: the token is stored only as a SHA-256, so the server cannot reproduce a link it has already handed out, and the create response deliberately carries none. Resending INVALIDATES the previous token — any link already circulated stops working. Put the returned token in the FRAGMENT of your invite URL (`/invite#<token>`), never in a path or query string: fragments are never sent to a server, so the token stays out of Referer headers, proxy access logs and browser history. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account. Keyed on the invitation id within THIS account, so an invitation belonging to another account, an unknown id, and an already-accepted, revoked or expired invitation are all the same 404. ROLE CEILING: the invitation's frozen role must be at or below your own — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise, so an admin cannot refresh an `owner` invitation issued by someone who outranked them. (Revoking one is deliberately NOT gated that way: revoking removes no role.)

`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}/resend` response.

 **This is the only place a plaintext invitation token is ever surfaced**, and it is
 surfaced to the inviter, who is an `admin` or `owner` of the account the invitation

 an id the caller obtained by listing their own account's invitations — and takes no

429.description: `INVITATION_RATE_LIMITED` — a resend MINTS a token, so it records one mint exactly as a create does and is counted by the same per-actor and per-account windows, one for one, with no exemption for the first resend. NOTE the ceilings are expressed in MINTS: because the create response carries no link, one usable invitation costs one create plus one resend, so the reachable rate of usable invitations is about half the stated ceiling

delete.description: Revoke a pending invitation. SOFT: the row is stamped `revoked_at`/ `revoked_by` and kept, never deleted, so the audit trail survives. Afterwards the token stops resolving and the address may be invited afresh. Requires account::members::manage AND account role `admin` or higher in THIS account. Keyed on the invitation id within THIS account, so a foreign, unknown or already-settled id is the same 404 — a second revoke included. There is deliberately NO role ceiling on revoke, unlike create and resend: revoking removes no role (the invitee holds nothing yet), so there is no standing to be above, and gating it would stop a lower-ranked admin cleaning up an `owner` invitation someone else left behind. Revoking withdraws the OFFER. It cannot withdraw a membership already created by an acceptance — remove the member instead (DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/members/{user_id}).

404.description: You are not a member of this account, or it does not exist; or the invitation does not exist, belongs to another account, or is already SETTLED (accepted, or already revoked). All INDISTINGUISHABLE. NOTE an EXPIRED but unsettled invitation is NOT in this set — it revokes with a 204, which makes revoke the one route on which "an expired invitation with this id exists here" differs from "no such id". That is not an oracle (reaching either requires being an admin of the account, who can already list its invitations) but it is a difference, and it is a decision rather than a surprise

post.description: Redeem an invitation token and join the account it names. AUTHENTICATED, but NOT account-scoped and NOT permission-gated: the redeemer is by definition not yet a member of the account, so the TOKEN is the capability. THE TOKEN GOES IN THE BODY. This operation declares no path, query or header parameter, deliberately — a token in a URL leaks through Referer headers, browser history, proxy access logs and screen shares. The invite link a client builds must carry the token in the URL FRAGMENT (`/invite#<token>`), which is never sent to a server; the SPA reads the fragment and POSTs it here. SIGNUP-THEN-ACCEPT: an invitee with no account should hold the token in memory (not in localStorage, not in the URL), register through POST /api/auth/register — which is UNCHANGED by this change and must never be given token handling — and then call this endpoint. If they register with a DIFFERENT address than the one invited, this endpoint returns the generic 404 below; that is correct, and the UI should say which address the invitation was sent to, which is safe to show to a holder of a valid token. INDISTINGUISHABLE FAILURES — THIS IS A CONTRACT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL: a wrong token, an expired token, an already-redeemed token, a revoked token, and a valid token presented by a user whose email does not match all return the SAME 404 with a BYTE-IDENTICAL body. Never add a distinguishing code or message for any of them — the difference is exactly what a token grinder wants, and `expired` alone confirms that a valid token once existed for that account. EMAIL BINDING: the authenticated user's email, normalized, must equal the invitation's. Emails are not verified in this deployment, so this is containment against a leaked link reaching the wrong logged-in tab, NOT proof of identity. Account membership is an implicit grant: a `member` holds at least Viewer on EVERY project, dataset and artifact in the account, an `admin` holds Editor on all of them, and an `owner` holds Owner — including delete, transfer and share — on projects they did not create. Adding, removing or re-roling a member changes all of that in one call.

requestBody.description:
`POST /api/account-invitations/accept` request (#146).

 **The token travels in the BODY, and nowhere else** (INV-18, research §4.2): a token in
 a URL path or query leaks through `Referer` headers, browser history, proxy access logs
 and screen shares. The link the invitee opens is a FRONTEND route carrying the token in
 the URL **fragment** (`/invite#<token>`) — fragments are never sent to a server — and the
 SPA reads it and POSTs it here.

 The route declares no path or query parameter at all, so this struct is the only place
 the token can arrive; a test asserts that against the SHIPPED `openapi.json` rather than
 against this comment.

201.description: Joined. Exactly one account_members row was created, the invitation was stamped accepted, and an audit row was written — all in one transaction.

200.description: You were ALREADY a member of that account. Idempotent: no second membership row, and your role is unchanged — an invitation never promotes an existing member. The invitation is consumed, so the token is now spent. `role` is your actual role, which may differ from the one the invitation named.

403.description: ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR — the person who sent this invitation no longer has the standing to confer it: they have been removed from the account, demoted below `admin`, or demoted below the role the invitation confers. The role ceiling is re-checked AT REDEMPTION, not only at issue, so an `owner` invitation from an owner who has since been demoted does not land days later. No membership is created and the invitation is left pending. Distinguishable from the 404 on purpose: you have already proved you hold a valid token addressed to you, so there is nothing left to enumerate.

404.description: INVALID_INVITATION — the one generic refusal. Returned identically, with a byte-identical body, for: no such token; an expired token; an already-redeemed token; a revoked token; and a valid token whose invited address does not match your account's email.

422.description: SEAT_LIMIT_REACHED — the account is at its plan's member allowance; `details` carries plan_id, limit and current so the UI can offer the upgrade path. Nothing is written and the invitation stays PENDING, so it can be redeemed once a seat frees. Or PERSONAL_ACCOUNT_NOT_MANAGEABLE — a personal account has exactly one member, its owner, and no membership surface.

bearerAuth.description: JWT obtained from POST /auth/login or POST /auth/register, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
`POST /api/account-invitations/accept` request (#146).

 **The token travels in the BODY, and nowhere else** (INV-18, research §4.2): a token in
 a URL path or query leaks through `Referer` headers, browser history, proxy access logs
 and screen shares. The link the invitee opens is a FRONTEND route carrying the token in
 the URL **fragment** (`/invite#<token>`) — fragments are never sent to a server — and the
 SPA reads it and POSTs it here.

 The route declares no path or query parameter at all, so this struct is the only place
 the token can arrive; a test asserts that against the SHIPPED `openapi.json` rather than
 against this comment.

token.description:
The base64url invitation token, exactly as it appeared in the invite link's
 fragment. Only its SHA-256 is ever compared against storage; the plaintext is never
 written anywhere.

AcceptInvitationResponse.description:
`POST /api/account-invitations/accept` response (#146).

 Deliberately minimal — the account id and the caller's role in it, which is what a
 client needs to switch into the account it just joined. Everything else arrives the way
 the rest of this module delivers state: a `SyncEntity::AccountMember` frame followed by
 the client's own `GET /api/accounts` (`account/sync.rs` — notify-and-refetch, no row
 data on the wire).

 `role` is the membership's ACTUAL role. On the idempotent already-a-member path (`200`
 rather than `201`) that is the role the caller already held, not the invitation's — an
 invitation never promotes an existing member (#146 DEC-12).

AcceptsEntry.description:
An `accepts` selector — a datatype id the converter consumes. Kept as a struct
 (not a bare string) so richer selectors (capabilities/subtypes) can be added
 without a wire break. ITEM-6 adds the supporting-file facets (role/slot/axis/kind/
 alignment), all `#[serde(default)]` so a bare `{type_id}` still parses as a PRIMARY
 input (back-compat, DEC-6).

alignment.description:
A declarative `Alignment` descriptor carried as open JSON so a manifest declares
 it verbatim (parses to `datatype::types::Alignment`). `None` for a primary input.

axis.description:
The primary datatype AXIS a supporting input aligns to (an `AxisSpec.name` —
 a generic axis NAME, never a fixed two-axis enum; DEC-6).

kind.description:
The supporting `kind` as an OPEN string (parses to `datatype::types::SupportingKind`),
 e.g. `annotation_table`. `None` for a primary input.

role.description:
The ROLE this input plays: `primary` (the dataset's main file) or `supporting`
 (an annotation aligned to an axis). Defaults to `primary` so an omitted `role`
 keeps a legacy `{type_id}` entry a primary input.

slot.description: The named upload SLOT this accept fills (the wizard drop-zone id), if any.

type_id.description: The exact datatype id accepted, e.g. `<package-namespace>/<type>`.

Account.description:
An `accounts` row. `personal_user_id` is the owning user for a `personal`
 account, `None` for an `organization` (enforced by the DB CHECK
 `accounts_personal_has_user`).

AccountKind.description:
What KIND of account this is (the personal/org discriminator, DEC-1). A text
 `kind` (not a boolean) so a third kind can be added without a schema change and
 so metering/billing read a stable, self-documenting discriminator.

oneOf.description:
The single, never-disabled account auto-created per user (owns their
 resources by default). Exactly one per user (INV-1).
A shared account many users join (the SaaS org). Created by A3 (`saas`).

AccountListResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts` response — the caller's account memberships (the switcher
 list). Owner-filtered by `list_user_accounts` (never a cross-account leak).

AccountMember.description:
An `account_members` row — one `(account, user)` membership edge with its
 coarse role. `PRIMARY KEY (account_id, user_id)` is the one-membership-per-pair
 constraint.

display_name.description:
The member's chosen display name (`users.display_name`, NULLABLE) — the
 preferred primary label when present. `None` ⇒ the UI falls back to `username`.

email.description: The member's email (`users.email`, NOT NULL) — the secondary identity line.

username.description:
The member's login handle (`users.username`, NOT NULL) — the UI's fallback
 primary label when `display_name` is absent. Enriches the response so a human
 reads a person, never the bare `user_id` UUID (#51 defect #1).

AccountMemberEvent.description:
One row of the membership audit ledger (#148), as served by the two read routes.

 **This is a projection, not the stored row.** The account-scoped route
 (`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/members/events`) applies three subtractions IN SQL, while
 the staff route (`GET /api/admin/accounts/{account_id}/members/events`) serves the full row:

 1. the unattended `system` event that SEEDS a new account is omitted — but NOT every
    `system` event: a membership that ended with no attributable human actor (for example
    because the user account itself was deleted) is a real event in this account and IS
    shown, as `actor_kind: system`;
 2. on platform-staff actions `actor_user_id` is NULL — you learn that staff acted, not
    which employee;
 3. `reason` is never selected.

 Applying them in SQL rather than in a serializer is why a later caller cannot reach a
 redacted column by constructing this struct differently.

 **This doc-comment is the SHIPPED schema description.** `JsonSchema` emits it verbatim into
 `openapi.json` and the generated `types.ts`, so a stale sentence here reaches every client —
 which is exactly how the first version of subtraction (1) went out contradicting the
 operation description in the same document, with the contract test green because it read
 only the operation half.

 **What it records, and what it does not.** A row exists for a membership mutation that
 COMMITTED. A refused attempt leaves nothing — the write shares the mutation's transaction,
 so a refusal rolls it back. Read this as "what happened to this account", never as "who
 tried what".

actor_kind.description:
`user` (a principal acting with no more authority than their own membership) |
 `admin` (a principal acting with the platform-staff capability, wherever that
 capability is checked — not merely a URL prefix) | `system` (no human actor is
 attributable: the provisioning hook, or a membership ended by the `users` FK cascade).
 Never absent — a staff action must be distinguishable from an owner's, and an
 unattributable one from both.

actor_user_id.description:
Who acted. NULL for a system action, and — on the ACCOUNT-scoped route only — NULL for
 a staff action too: an account admin learns that platform staff acted, not which
 employee. The staff identity is stored and is served on the admin surface.

invitation_id.description: Ties an `invited` event to the `joined` that answered it.

old_role.description:
Both present on `role_changed`; `old_role` alone on a removal; `new_role` alone on a
 join.

reason.description: Staff-authored note. Always absent on the account-scoped route (#148 DEC-7).

target_email.description:
The invitation address, for an invitee who has no account yet. Trimmed and otherwise
 stored verbatim (it is NOT lowercased — the local part is case-sensitive and this row is
 permanent). Mutually exclusive with `target_user_id` by CHECK constraint.

target_user_id.description:
Whom it happened to. NULL only for an invitation sent to an ADDRESS that has no user
 yet — an invitation to somebody already in the directory names them by id instead, and
 then carries no address. Exactly one of `target_user_id` and `target_email` is set, for
 every action.

AccountMemberEventsResponse.description:
The membership-audit read response — paged with the same numbered settings-list idiom as
 [`AccountMembersResponse`], so a client pages both surfaces identically.

AccountMembersManageContext.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/members/manage-context` response (#139) — the
 caller's member-management standing in ONE account.

 Reaching this response at all IS the authorization proof: it is served behind
 `AccountScope<RoleAdmin>`, so the caller has been shown to hold
 `account::members::manage` AND to rank `admin` or above in THIS account. It is the
 preflight a management UI runs before rendering write affordances — the global
 `usePermission(Permissions.AccountMembersManage)` answers only half the question.

account_id.description:
The account this answer is about — echoes the PATH id, never the
 `X-Account-Id` header (which is ignored on this surface; DEC-1).

actor_role.description: The caller's REAL role in this account (`admin` or `owner` here, by the floor).

member_count.description: How many members the account currently has.

AccountMembersResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{id}/members` response — one org's members, paged (the
 settings-list numbered-pagination idiom; `total` drives "Showing N of M").

AccountRole.description:
The acting user's COARSE role on an account (DEC / INV-4). `Ord` is
 `Owner > Admin > Member` (derived from declaration order below), so
 [`AccountRole::allows`] grades a minimum-role floor. Distinct from the
 within-resource ACL `EffectivePermission` (viewer/editor).

AckResponse.description:
Uniform ack for the agent up-endpoints. `ok: false` means the request did
 not correlate to something owned by the caller — a `request_id` with no
 pending dispatch (already resolved / timed out / never existed / owned by
 another user), or a `connection_id` that is no longer the caller's bound
 control connection. Not an error the engine needs to retry, just
 informational.

ActionContribution.description:
A manifest-contributed interaction ACTION (S4).

 The DECLARATION layer only — the emitter still owns how each dialect compiles,
 because the emitted source is the attested artifact and a manifest must never be
 able to inject python. A package therefore picks from the dialects this build
 ships; declaring an unknown one is a boot-time lint failure, not a silently
 uncapturable action.

action_type.description:
The dotted action type the client posts to `POST /provenance/actions`,
 e.g. `gate.commit`. Must not collide with a built-in action type.

dispatchable.description:
Whether the interaction chokepoint captures it. A `false` entry RESERVES the
 vocabulary without dispatching it (mirroring the built-in `annotate.*`).

fidelity.description: How faithfully a capture of this action reproduces.

recipe.description:
The recipe SHAPE this action posts, which selects the code emitter. Required
 for a `dispatchable` action (there is nothing to attest to without one).

ActionFidelity.description:
How faithfully a captured action reproduces. Mirrors
 `provenance::action_registry::FidelityClass` (declared HERE so the manifest layer
 does not depend on the higher-order provenance module).

oneOf.description: A declarative predicate/recipe — fully re-executable code.
An identity/label operation.
A view-only gesture (no data mutation).

ActionRecipeDialect.description:
The recipe SHAPES this build can compile into a reproducible `select(ctx)`
 script. Each names a payload shape, never a domain: the emitter reads the shape
 and answers one boolean per element of the selected axis.

oneOf.description:
`{criteria: [{column, control?, min?, max?, keep?}]}` — the AND-ed
 threshold/keep-set list.
`{col, op, val}` — one allow-listed comparator against one column.
`{column_ref, labels}` — membership of a column in a label set.
`{ids}` — an explicit element-id allow-list.
`{coords_ref, polygon}` — a polygon over a pinned 2-D projection.
`{op, refs}` — a set operation combining named prior selections.

AnalysisContributionData.description:
ONE `contributes.analyses[]` entry, as far as the BACKEND is concerned (S3).

 The block is authored for the FE (`ProcessorManifestData`) and the backend has no
 business re-typing it, so every other key rides `rest` verbatim and re-serializes
 unchanged — `GET /api/extensions` stays byte-faithful and the FE (which reads the
 RAW manifest text over `GET /api/processors/packages`) is untouched.

 What the backend DOES read is `id` (an analysis run's `generator_id`) and the
 `methods` narration block below.

draftable.description:
The `draftable` block (draftable-entity ITEM-9), TYPED on the wire so the FE
 analysis-contribution schema carries it (`types.ts` gets `draftable?:
 DraftableSpec`) — the FE mount uses it to detect a draftable editor view. It is
 pulled out of `rest` (so it is not double-serialized) and parsed LENIENTLY: a
 malformed block is logged + treated as absent (the `run()` precedent), never
 wedging the analysis. The loader stays DOMAIN-BLIND (INV-1): `kind`/`freeze`/
 `edit`/`freeze_on` are opaque strings it carries, never interprets.

env.description:
The analysis-domain ENV IMAGE this analysis' compute runs inside (#189) — the
 analysis-side twin of [`ConverterContribution::env`], same manifest key, same
 grammar, same one-level-above-`run:` placement (DEC-1).

 `None` ⇒ the deployment default resolves exactly as it did before this field
 existed, so an analysis that declares no `env` is byte-identical to today
 (INV-1). Pulled out of `rest` so it is not double-serialized, mirroring
 `draftable`; with `skip_serializing_if` the wire is unchanged for a manifest
 that omits it (INV-5).

 **Parsed STRICTLY, unlike `draftable`.** A malformed env-id is rejected here
 naming the key and the value, never warn-and-ignored: a lenient parse would
 drop the declaration and silently run the analysis against the DEPLOYMENT
 DEFAULT image — presenting to the user as "the analysis is broken" while the
 real cause is a typo'd env-id that nothing reported (INV-2). The same value is
 rejected earlier and more loudly by the build lint
 (`build_helper/processor_manifest.rs`), which the loader runs BEFORE this parse
 and whose failure is `tracing::error!`-logged and collected into the package's
 `PackageLoadStatus.error`.

id.description: The analysis id — the `generator_id` a run of this analysis records.

methods.description:
How a run of this analysis is NARRATED in the exported methods section (S3).
 Absent ⇒ the generic sentence.

AnalysisParameters.description:
The analysis parameters: the decision day and the baseline window end
 (2026-10-19 contract: a draw is baseline when day ≤ `baseline_max_day`;
 pre-treatment negative days count as baseline). Per-analysis user inputs
 (screen B/C), never operational tunables (DEC-9); defaults apply when the
 UI omits the block.

ArrayAttr.description:
One typed ATTRIBUTE (a measured/dependent value) an array carries (INV-7). `dtype`
 is an OPEN string (`f32`/`i64`/`bool`/`categorical`/`str`/…) — the physical decoder
 maps the ones it knows; an unrecognized dtype is carried verbatim, never a parse
 error (the `SupportingKind::Other` open-vocabulary discipline, applied to attrs).

dtype.description: The attribute's declared dtype (open string), e.g. `f32`, `i64`, `bool`, `categorical`.

name.description: The attribute name (a table column / a sparse array's value name / an edge attr).

ArrayDecl.description:
One ARRAY a datatype declares over an OPEN axis set (INV-7 / R4 §4). This is the
 generalization the whole lifecycle turns on: instead of ONE implicit `storage`
 array over a FIXED pair of axes (all a two-axis store can hold), a datatype declares
 a LIST of named arrays, each binding its `dims` to declared axes (or an anonymous
 `k`), carrying typed `attrs`, and owning its OWN physical `layout`.
 So a `(cluster,cluster)` graph, a `(comparison,item)` statistics table, or a
 `(set,item)` membership — none of which fit that fixed pair — become first-class
 declared arrays.

 The serve layer reads NONE of this — not `kind`, not `layout`. `/data[/{*member}]`
 resolves a member path and a byte range and hands the bytes over; the client decodes
 from the artifact's producer-declared `structure` (ITEM-12 / INV-1). What an
 `ArrayDecl` is FOR is declaration + viewer dispatch. `deny_unknown_fields` makes a
 typo'd array field fail at manifest parse (the separability-gate discipline).

attrs.description: The typed attributes this array carries (table columns / value name / edge attrs).

dims.description: The array's dims, each bound to a declared axis or an anonymous `k` (open axis set).

kind.description:
The SEMANTIC array kind (OPEN string: `matrix`/`graph`/`projection`/`annotation-table`/…
 — a contributed datatype names its own) — the dim-signature/viewer dispatch key.
 NEVER a serve-core branch (DEC-4 split).

name.description: The array name within its datatype (`X`, `abstracted_graph`, `membership`, `logFC`, …).

ArrayDim.description:
One DIMENSION binding of a declared array (INV-7 / open-axis). A dim binds either
 to a named entity AXIS (an [`AxisSpec::name`] — the join-keyed dimension) OR to an
 anonymous positional latent extent `k` (a 2..50-wide projection's second dim, whose
 positions are ordinals and own no join key).
 Untagged so a manifest writes the two forms verbatim as R4 declares them —
 `{ axis: cluster }` XOR `{ k: 2 }` — and a `{}`/typo matches neither variant and
 errors at parse (the exactly-one guard falls out of the untagged encoding).

anyOf.description: Bound to a declared entity AXIS (an `AxisSpec.name`: `rows`/`cluster`/`comparison`/…).
An anonymous positional latent extent (`k`) — a projection's dims, no join key.

dataset_id.description:
Dataset (owner) tenancy scope (the datasets-management processing path).
 NULL for a project-scoped artifact. Exactly one of `project_id`/`dataset_id`
 is set on a live artifact (ITEM-23).

datatype.description: Opaque to the host; validated against P2's registry.

hidden.description:
Excluded from catalog/picker LISTINGS (still fetchable by id) — set on
 derived alternate-representation artifacts (ITEM-20).

is_multifile.description: Whether `object_key` points at a manifest (members resolved through it).

logical_bytes.description:
The size the data REPRESENTS when materialised — the number a user reads as
 "Size", and the only one that belongs in a byte total on screen. Equals
 `stored_bytes` for an artifact that owns a blob; `rows × element width` for a
 gathered one.

 `None` means genuinely UNKNOWN, not zero. It is an `Option` so that every
 consumer — and, through the generated TypeScript, every UI consumer — has to
 decide what to show when there is no answer. Rendering `0 Bytes` for a
 500,000-row gathered column is the defect this type prevents.

meta.description: Producer-declared: what the artifact means, for display. Same contract.

object_key.description:
The data blob key (single-file) or the manifest blob key (multi-file) —
 or `None` when this artifact has NO STORED BYTES (ITEM-16).

 `None` is not "unknown" and not "empty": it means the row is GATHERED, and
 `structure.gathered_from` carries the recipe that produces the bytes on
 demand. The `artifacts_bytes_or_recipe` CHECK constraint enforces that
 exactly one of the two is present, so a reader may treat `None` as a
 GUARANTEE that the recipe is there rather than as a case to guess about.

 Every consumer of this field must decide what a gathered artifact means for
 it. There is deliberately no `unwrap_or_default()` anywhere: an empty object
 key is a valid-looking address that resolves to nothing, which is the
 antipattern `202608040002_artifact_model_drop.sql` removed from four other
 columns. Sites that cannot yet serve a gathered artifact return a named
 refusal citing the ITEM that owes the real behaviour.

project_id.description:
Project tenancy scope (the P11 workbench path). NULL for a dataset-scoped
 artifact (ITEM-23): an artifact is scoped to a project OR a dataset (owner).

representation_of.description:
The source artifact this row is an alternate encoding of (ITEM-20); NULL
 for a first-class artifact.

role.description:
Producer-declared TIER (DEC-8): `artifact` = promotable/exportable,
 `intermediate` = viz-only. A first-class column for the same reason `hidden`
 is one — it is a property the SERVER acts on (the promote gate), not display
 data. It is deliberately NOT re-derived from `meta`: `meta` is the producer's
 declaration carried verbatim, and reading operational meaning out of it would
 restate in another column exactly what dropping `params` (ITEM-7) removed.
 Never empty, and NOT because a blank is normalized here: a blank or omitted
 `role` is REFUSED upstream by `sandbox::outputs::deserialize_declared_role`,
 and this struct carries no `#[serde(default)]`. The former `role_or_default`
 mapped blank → `artifact` — blank ⇒ the PROMOTABLE tier — and was deleted
 rather than fixed, so absence cannot resolve to a privilege (INV-2).

run_id.description: The producing run; null for source/upload artifacts.

status.description:
`pending|ready|failed`. `failed` is also what the post-ingest conformance
 gate (ITEM-18 / DEC-12) writes when an artifact's bytes disagree with its
 declared `structure`.

stored_bytes.description:
Bytes written to the OBJECT STORE — 0 for a gathered artifact, which owns no
 blob, and that 0 is the correct storage answer. The only reader that wants this
 is the provenance export (its size cap and `fetch.txt`). It is emphatically NOT
 a display size: see [`Self::logical_bytes`].

structure.description:
Producer-declared: how to decode the bytes. The server stores and serves
 this; it never interprets it. No default — an artifact whose producer
 declared no structure is an error at ingest, not an empty object.

ArtifactBytesRow.description:
One artifact the report has something to say about.

 Only rows whose bytes are NOT confirmed present appear here — a report that listed
 every row would be indistinguishable from one that checked nothing. The counts on
 [`BytesPresenceReport`] carry the rest.

content_hash.description: The artifact's content identity, so an operator restoring a store can match it up.

detail.description:
A plain-language explanation naming what is not here. Says the bytes are not in
 this store; never asserts that anything removed them.

output_id.description: The producer's own id for this output — how a user recognises it.

ArtifactCatalog.description: One artifact enriched with its datatype meaning.

datatype.description:
The resolved datatype descriptor; `null` when the datatype is not registered
 (fail-soft — a stale / uninstalled-extension datatype).

unknown.description: `true` when the datatype is unknown (the FE renders a generic "unknown" card).

viewers.description: Viewers resolved UP the lattice (empty when unknown).

ArtifactFilter.description: Filters for the catalog list endpoint (all optional).

capability.description: Match any artifact whose datatype advertises this capability (via P2's registry).

on_axis.description:
Match any artifact DECLARING A MEMBERSHIP on this axis — the axis's identity, i.e.
 its key artifact's `key_sequence_digest` (dimension-membership ITEM-29).

 INV-2's *"an indexed catalog match"*: the pane resolves its anchor to one or more axis
 identities and narrows the candidate set to the artifacts that declare something about
 that axis, using the GIN index `202608040004` builds for exactly this containment.

 It NARROWS the candidate set; it does not decide the offer. Which candidate is offered
 stays the client's A1/A2/A3/A4 judgment over identity, absence and intersection — a
 judgment SQL cannot express and, pushed into SQL, would sit somewhere no unit test can
 reach. The two are not redundant: this filter can only test declared containment.

 The value is an OPAQUE digest string, matched whole. It is never parsed, split or
 pattern-matched (INV-4).

subtypes_of.description:
Match any artifact whose datatype `is_a` this supertype (the Galaxy lattice
 rule) — resolved to a concrete id set via P2's registry in the handler. Drives
 the Tier-2 artifact-ref picker (P2 ITEM-20/22).

ArtifactNodeDto.description: An artifact node (from P1's `artifacts` catalog) — a graph vertex.

promotable.description:
True when this artifact may be promoted to a standalone dataset — i.e. its
 datatype is a dataset INPUT the upload pipeline can expand into a full
 linked-object dataset (`extensions::is_dataset_input`). The UI gates the
 Promote affordance on this; a component-object artifact is `false`.

run_id.description: The producing run; null for source/upload/reference roots.

AuthProviderResponse.description:
Admin-view summary of an auth provider. The `config` JSONB is
 returned with `client_secret` and any sensitive key contents
 MASKED — see handlers.rs::mask_provider_config.

last_test_at.description: When the admin last clicked Test on this row (null = never).

last_test_message.description: Human-readable detail from the last test.

last_test_ok.description: Outcome of the last test (null = never tested).

AxisSpec.description:
A named ENTITY AXIS a datatype declares (ITEM-3 / DEC-15). A primary datatype
 declares its OWN axes and there is no core-blessed pair: a tabular type declares
 `rows`+`columns`, an image stack `frames`+`channels`, an assay type whichever two
 (or three) entity axes IT measures over — each of those is just a contributed
 datatype's DATA, and the core sees no difference between them.
 OPEN + generic: the core knows only "an axis has a name + a key label", never what
 the axis REPRESENTS. Supporting files align to an axis by `name`; the alignment
 engine, the integrate converter, and the axis-tagged annotation-column output they
 produce are all axis-agnostic. Contributable via a manifest AND attachable to an
 existing Rust datatype (the loader merges axes onto the registry entry).

 The list is an IDENTITY LIST and its ORDER MEANS NOTHING. The one role a consumer
 needs — which axis is the ENTITY axis — is declared separately and by NAME, on
 [`Datatype::entity_axis`]; see there for why reading it off position 0 was a leak and
 what it got wrong. Do not re-privilege a position here.

key_label.description:
The human label for this axis's entity KEY, e.g. `Row ID`, `Channel name` —
 shown in the add-supporting-file form + used as the key-column detection hint.

name.description: The axis name a supporting file / selector references, e.g. `rows`, `columns`.

AxisSummary.description:
One declared AXIS of the project, with its cardinality. The open-axis replacement
 for the retired `(n_cells, n_genes)` scalar pair: `name` is a DECLARED
 `AxisSpec.name` (`cells`/`genes`/`region`/`comparison`/`cluster`/…), never an
 obs/var enum (DEC-6). A `(comparison, gene)` DE table or a `(cluster, cluster)`
 graph has no obs/var home, so two scalars could never describe one.

content_hash.description:
**The axis's IDENTITY** — the `content_hash` of the key artifact that IS this
 axis (INV-3). This is the field a client keys on; [`AxisSummary::name`] is a
 display label and two different axes may legitimately carry the same one.

 Without it on the wire, two same-label axes are indistinguishable to a consumer
 and the only way to render them is to fold them back together by name — i.e. to
 re-create, in the client, the identity confusion this field exists to remove.

key_sequence_digest.description:
The ORDERED KEY SEQUENCE this axis IS, by its digest — the key artifact's own
 `structure.key_sequence_digest` (dimension-membership ITEM-31).

 Two identities for one axis, and they are not redundant: `content_hash` identifies
 the ARTIFACT (it is what `$scope.axis` carries and what a client keys a pane on),
 while this is the identity a PRODUCER can name about itself — a producer cannot name
 a `content_hash` (ingest mints it, after the fact, over bytes the producer has not
 finished writing), so the only identity a declaration can carry is this one.

 It pins an axis to a SEQUENCE rather than to a length. Two axes of equal `n` whose
 keys are in different orders are not the same axis, and any read that addresses one
 axis positionally through another is only sound while the digests agree. It rides the
 catalog so a client can ask the membership question WITHOUT first fetching every
 artifact to find the digest: `ArtifactFilter.on_axis` takes the digest, the client
 holds only the `content_hash`, and resolving one to the other out of the artifact
 list would mean fetching the very list the filter exists to narrow.

 `None` when the key artifact declares none — an axis whose alignment nothing can join
 on, a legitimate state (A3), not an error. A consumer that needs the guarantee must
 treat `None` as "cannot be checked", never as "matches".

length.description:
The number of entries on this axis, as its own key artifact DECLARED it. Always
 one artifact's own `structure.n` — never a value computed across artifacts.

name.description: The declared axis LABEL, for display. Never a key (INV-3).

BytesPresenceReport.description:
A project's artifact-bytes report.

 `checked` is every row examined; the three counters partition it. **`absent > 0` is a
 STORAGE observation, not a verdict on the artifacts** — the catalog rows are untouched
 and still `ready`, and they become readable again the moment their bytes are back.

indeterminate.description:
Rows the store could not answer for. Deliberately its own counter rather than being
 folded into `absent`: "I could not look" and "it is not here" are different facts,
 and only one of them is about your data.

Cardinality.description: The declared cardinality of a `produces` output (ITEM-10 / DEC-18).

oneOf.description: Exactly one instance.
Zero or one instance.
Zero or more instances.

CatalogueEnv.description:
The benchmark container-image reference the catalogue carries as DATA (the
 runtime `EnvRef` is built from `method-env-images.json` — a different
 artifact; see the PLAN's env note). The image string carries no scheme and is
 never fetched by this module.

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Self-service password change for the authenticated user. Requires
 the current password as proof. Only valid for local-password
 accounts (`password_hash IS NOT NULL`).

Contributes.description:
The contribution kinds an extension adds. `datatypes` is now ACTIVE (ITEM-1 /
 DEC-19/DEC-20-amended): an extension folder contributes DOMAIN datatypes — its own
 namespaced types, `annotation-table`, whatever a future field needs — that the
 loader MERGES into the datatype registry alongside the Rust-registered lattice
 roots. A new domain is a new `extensions/<id>/` folder with ZERO core edit, which
 is precisely why the core names no domain of its own.

actions.description:
INTERACTION ACTIONS this extension adds to the provenance capture vocabulary
 (S4). Before this, `provenance::action_registry::catalog()` was a CLOSED
 code-defined list: a package shipping a new user gesture could not have it
 captured without a server rebuild. A contributed action names the recipe
 DIALECT it posts, and the emitter compiles it with the same domain-free
 `select(ctx)` machinery the built-in actions use — so the recorded
 `code_sha256` attests to a real, runnable script for a contributed action too.

analyses.description:
The FE analysis contributions (`ProcessorManifestData`), carried through
 LOSSLESSLY (see [`AnalysisContributionData`]) so `GET /api/extensions` stays
 byte-faithful, while the backend reads the ONE sub-block it owns: the
 declarative METHODS narration (S3).

datatypes.description:
Datatype declarations merged into the datatype registry (ITEM-1/2). Core
 ROOT/abstract types (`data`/`tabular`/`matrix`) stay Rust-registered; DOMAIN
 datatypes are manifest-contributed here (DEC-20-amended).

sections.description:
VISUALIZE-PANE SECTIONS this package contributes (ITEM-1). A section is a
 declarative `view_spec` rendering as one block inside a shared pane's single
 scroll track — its own first-class contribution kind, NOT an analysis carrying
 a flag (DEC-1) and NOT a view: it registers into the FE's `registry.sections`
 slot and therefore never reaches `placeViews` / `viewAutomountGate` /
 `assertContributableArea`. The centre reservation is unreachable from this path
 by construction.

 Additive by the same rule every other key here follows — `#[serde(default)]`,
 so every manifest that predates sections parses byte-identically.

ConvertQuery.description: Query for a host-lite conversion (`from`/`to` datatype-or-format keys).

from.description: The source format/datatype key of a declared converter (e.g. `file/csv`).

to.description:
The target datatype (e.g. `columnar-table` — the target of the one near-term
 host-lite converter, `csv/tsv → columnar-table`).

ConvertResult.description: The result of a host-lite conversion.

result.description: The converted payload (a `{columns, rows}` table for the columnar-table layout).

ConverterContribution.description: A converter contribution: an accepts→produces transform run in a sandbox.

accepts.description: Input datatype selectors this converter accepts.

env.description:
The analysis-domain ENV IMAGE this converter's compute runs inside
 (ITEM-23 / DEC-22/23). An env-id resolved by the sandbox `env_image`
 registry (`env-id → {oci_ref, digest}`), lazy-fetched on first use.
 The registry resolves ANY declared env-id to a per-env image repo — the set
 is deployment data, not a list this type knows.

 `None` ⇒ the DEPLOYMENT DEFAULT (`env_image::default_env_id`: the
 `CYTO_SANDBOX_ENV_ID` override, else the admin settings row, else the union of
 the envs the loaded registry declares). There is **no embedded-rootfs
 fallback** — this doc claimed one until #189, and the claim was false:
 the embedded rootfs was removed when DEC-24 was reversed (see the `env_image` module
 doc, "nothing embedded"), and a run that resolves NO env-id is a hard
 `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` 503 at `local_bwrap.rs` / `service.rs`, not a silent
 fallback. The stale promise mattered: it described the exact
 substitute-and-continue behaviour that INV-2 forbids, so a reader could
 reasonably have built one.

 Parsed strictly — see [`de_checked_env`] for why a malformed env-id may not be
 warn-and-ignored.

id.description: Stable converter id (unique within the extension).

params.description: Parameter declaration. `"none"` for a zero-param converter (this round).

produces.description: The declared, static SUPERSET of outputs (the run emits the actual 0..N).

run.description: How the converter runs (sandbox / runtime / entry script).

trigger.description: When the converter fires. This round the vocabulary is `on-ingest` (DEC-4).

entry.description: The host-lite converter key or the sandbox entrypoint; `None` for a pure marker.

oneOf.description: In-process, host-lite (P3-independent) — e.g. `csv → columnar-table`.

Via P3's sandbox JobRunner — e.g. a heavyweight container-format convert that
 needs the analysis environment's reader libraries (deferred, ITEM-18).

One covariate column's numeric-ness fact (an inspect-time report: a
 covariate known to a numeric rule is a usable covariate; a text column is
 a covariate the engine cannot use as a number).

CovariateFacts.description:
The covariate facts of a saved model: the catalogue's mode + whether the
 run actually ran with covariates on (both recorded at save — the J screen's
 "uses age" is `used`, never a re-derivation).

CovariateMode.description: Whether a method's inputs include patient covariates beyond the markers.

Coverage.description:
Per-patient coverage aggregate (no per-patient payload in the response —
 coverage facts only).

CreateAuthProviderResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /admin/auth-providers`. Wraps the persisted
 row in an envelope so we can attach a `connection_warning` when a
 create-time probe failed and the row was auto-downgraded to
 `enabled=false`. Mirrors `llm_repository`'s create-response shape.

connection_warning.description:
Populated when the provider was created with `enabled=true` but
 the connection probe failed; the row is persisted with
 `enabled=false` and this carries the failure reason so the UI
 can render an inline warning. `null` on the happy path.

CreateDatasetRequest.description: Create-dataset request body (metadata-only; files land via upload/promote).

datatype.description: Optional pre-known datatype (the upload path sets it from the sniffer).

parent_frozen_artifact_id.description:
The frozen artifact this draft is a FORK of (INV-7 / DEC-11). When set, the new draft
 is born (still `open`) with its `frozen_artifact_id` pointing at this prior version, so
 the next freeze records it as the new artifact's `parent_artifact_id` — the SAME edge
 the freeze-completion hook reads for a reopened draft. This is what makes the frozen-view
 "Edit → new version" fork link into the lineage chain (the editor forks a NEW draft rather
 than reopening the source, so the parent must be threaded explicitly). Must reference an
 artifact in `project_id` (a foreign/nonexistent artifact → 422). Absent for a fresh
 New-collection draft (version 1, no parent).

email.description:
The address to invite. Normalized (`lower(trim(…))`) before anything is done with
 it; an empty/whitespace-only value is a 400.

role.description:
The account role the invitation will confer. Must be at or below the caller's own
 role in this account — 403 `ROLE_ABOVE_ACTOR` otherwise (R-1, #142).

CreateInvitationResponse.description:
`POST /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — **the same three bytes in
 every case**.

 `202 Accepted` with `{"status":"sent"}` whether the address belongs to no user, to a
 user, to a user who is already a member of this account, or already has a live
 invitation. The last two are server-side no-ops. The body is assembled from a single
 `const` in `handlers.rs`, so no branch can vary it.

 The `status` field exists only so the response is a JSON object rather than an empty
 body — a client that wants to branch on the outcome cannot, and that is the point.

CreateJobRequest.description:
Create-job request. `params` is opaque to the scheduler and passed through to
 the runner.

dataset_id.description:
Owning dataset id (ITEM-23 / DEC-scope): a data-processing run is
 OWNER-scoped to a dataset (no project). When set, a
 `job_scope(scope_kind='dataset')` row is persisted at create (ITEM-68) so
 the finalize ingest tags the produced `artifacts.dataset_id` with this
 dataset. Mutually exclusive with `project_id` (a job is project- OR
 dataset-scoped, not both — the create handler rejects both as
 `AMBIGUOUS_JOB_SCOPE`).

priority_class.description:
Requested priority class (`interactive|normal|batch`). Absent → the server
 infers from the trigger; an unknown value clamps to `normal`.

project_id.description:
Owning project id (analysis jobs; drives ingest scoping). When set, a
 `job_scope(scope_kind='project')` row is persisted at create (ITEM-68).

CreateOrganizationRequest.description:

DataRangeQuery.description:
`?range=` — the byte-span query parameter (artifact-model ITEM-36).

 The URL is the cache key. A `Range:` HEADER yields a `206`, which browsers

DatasetArtifactGroup.description:
One (dataset, datatype) group of artifacts, plus ONE representative member's
 producer declarations for a contributed preview to read.

 # How the representative is chosen — and why it is no longer the biggest

 The representative exists to hand a preview ONE member's `meta` + `structure`. What
 makes a member a good one is therefore its DECLARATION, so that is what the rule is
 about. In order:

 1. **it declares a `structure`** — the half a preview usually needs (dimensions live
    there). A member declaring `{}` cannot describe the group to anyone.
 2. **it declares a `meta`** — same reason, second because it is the half a preview
    can more often do without.
 3. **it is the most recent** (`created_at DESC`) — among members that declare equally
    well, the current producer's statement is the group's statement.
 4. **`output_id` then `id`** — a total order, so the rule always names exactly one row.

 This replaced `ORDER BY size_bytes DESC, id`, which the previous version of this
 comment named for what it was: *a size rule, not a semantic one*. The magnitude of a
 byte count decided whose declaration shipped, which is incidental; and every tie fell
 through to `id`, which is `gen_random_uuid()` — so two ingests of the SAME data, with
 the same sizes, picked different representatives at random. Steps 1-2 make the rule
 about the thing it is for, and steps 3-4 make it reproducible.

 The three aggregates in `artifact_summary_rows` must all order by this identical
 clause: the group ships ONE member's declarations, and pairing one row's `meta` with
 another's `structure` describes an artifact that does not exist.

Their combined LOGICAL size — the size the data represents, which is what a

 Rows whose logical size is UNKNOWN contribute nothing (SQL `sum` skips NULL)

The arrays this datatype declares OVER its axes (INV-7 / open-axis DATA). Empty
 for a single-implicit-array datatype (its `storage` IS its one array); a
 COMPOSITE kind (trajectory / set-membership / graph / statistics-table) declares
 its multiple arrays here, each self-describing (`dims`→axes, typed `attrs`, its
 own `layout`).
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps the wire back-compatible — an omitted `arrays` parses empty.

axes.description:
The entity AXES this datatype declares (ITEM-3 / DEC-15) — a generic, OPEN
 field a manifest contributes AND the loader can merge onto an existing Rust
 datatype. Empty for datatypes with no aligned axes. `#[serde(default)]` keeps
 the wire back-compatible (an omitted `axes` parses as empty).

entity_axis.description:
WHICH of this datatype's [`axes`](Self::axes) is its ENTITY axis — the axis whose
 entries a value of this datatype has exactly ONE PER, i.e. the axis a read of one
 of its artifacts is dense over. Names an `AxisSpec.name` this datatype declares.

 ── WHY IT IS DECLARED AND NOT POSITIONAL ───────────────────────────────────────

 This exists because the client used to take `axes[0]` — the FIRST declared axis —
 as the entity axis, which is a semantic [`AxisSpec`] itself disclaims ("the core
 knows only that an axis has a name + a key label, never what the axis
 REPRESENTS"). `axes` is an IDENTITY LIST: it says which axes exist, in no
 meaningful order, so position 0 carries no more meaning than position 2.

 It was also already WRONG on declared data, in two shapes:
   - a microscopy image declaring four axes of which THREE are raster dimensions
     resolved a raster dimension as its entity axis, when the entity axis is the
     segmented-object one it declares LAST;
   - two CONTRIBUTED composite kinds declare their axes in one order while their
     PRIMARY array binds them in the other, so a column of either is dense over
     the axis declared SECOND. (This doc-comment ships verbatim inside the
     OpenAPI contract, so it may not name the two ids — compare each `axes:`
     block with the `dims:` of the array below it in the contributed manifests.)
 Nothing surfaced either: an entity-axis mistake reports a plausible number.

 ── WHY NOT `arrays[0].dims[0]` ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

 [`ArrayDecl::dims`] IS positional (row-major storage order), so it looks like the
 answer — but it answers a different question: "the first STORAGE dimension of the
 primary array". For an image those differ (the primary array is the raster; the
 entity axis is `region`), and most datatypes declare no `arrays` at all. So the
 entity axis is declared directly.

 `None` is honest silence, NOT a default: a consumer resolving this reads the SOLE
 axis when the datatype declares exactly one (there is no choice to make), and
 otherwise gets no answer at all rather than a positional guess.
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps the wire back-compatible (an omitted key parses `None`).

labels.description:
OPTIONAL per-column DISPLAY LABELS, keyed by column name — `{ <column>:
 "<display label>" }` (ITEM-14 / DEC-4). Carried verbatim from
 [`DatatypeContribution::labels`](crate::modules::extensions::types::DatatypeContribution)
 and served on `GET /api/datatypes`, which is what populates the FE registry the
 consumer reads (`WorkbenchDataSource`'s `columnLabel` dep is
 `datatypeRegistry.get(id)?.labels?.[name]`).

 It is the ONE surviving piece of the deleted `axes[].annotations` forecast, because a
 raw column name → a human label is the one fact about a column that is NOT derivable
 from the data. It is a LOOKUP, not a schema claim: silent for a column it does not
 mention, so — unlike the list it replaced — it can never assert that a column exists.
 That is why it coexists with INV-5 rather than contradicting it.

 This field had NO Rust home for three rounds: the manifest declared it, the TS mirror
 declared it and the FE read it, but `to_datatype()` had nothing to copy it into, so the
 value was permanently `undefined` at its only consumer. Do not remove it without
 removing the consumer, the TS mirror and the build-gate mirror in the same change —
 a half-present lookup is worse than none, because it looks wired.
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps the wire back-compatible — an omitted `labels` parses empty.

DatatypeContribution.description:
A manifest-contributed datatype (ITEM-1/2 / DEC-19). Mirrors the Rust `Datatype`
 shape but carries only the fields a data-only manifest declares; the loader converts
 it into a full [`Datatype`] (defaulting the host-only fields — selectors, viewers,
 converters) and MERGES it into the datatype registry. A declarative `schema`
 (JSON-schema) replaces a Rust fn-pointer validator for manifest datatypes (DEC-21).

 `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` is scoped to `DatatypeContribution` + its sub-structs
 ONLY (NOT `Contributes` / `ExtensionManifest`): the SAME `manifest.yaml` is dual-parsed
 by the backend and the FE, each ignoring the other's top-level keys, so whole-manifest
 denial would reject every real package's FE `analyses:` block at boot (DEC-4). Denial
 HERE catches a typo'd datatype-contribution field at parse time.

arrays.description:
The arrays this datatype declares OVER its axes (INV-7 / open-axis DATA). A
 COMPOSITE kind (set-membership / graph / statistics-table / trajectory) declares
 its multiple arrays here;
 carried verbatim onto `Datatype.arrays`. Reuses the core `ArrayDecl` (which owns
 `deny_unknown_fields`), so a typo'd array field fails at manifest parse.

axes.description:
The entity AXES this datatype declares (ITEM-3) — e.g. the axis a
 supporting-aligned type carries, or a primary type's own entity axes.

 IDENTITY ONLY (`name`, `key_label`). An axis no longer enumerates the columns a
 dataset "would" carry: that list was an unverified forecast, and on one real
 imported dataset 8 of the 9 declared annotations did not exist while 64 of the
 dataset's 65 columns went undeclared. Column types are read from the artifacts
 that actually landed, each of which stamps its own kind — a fact the conformance
 gate verifies.

entity_axis.description:
WHICH declared axis is this datatype's ENTITY axis — the axis whose entries a
 value of this type has ONE PER, i.e. the axis a read of one of its artifacts is
 dense over. Must name one of the `axes` above; carried verbatim onto
 [`Datatype::entity_axis`](crate::modules::datatype::types::Datatype::entity_axis),
 which documents why it is DECLARED rather than taken from a position.

 Omit it for a single-axis datatype (there is no choice to make). A MULTI-axis
 datatype that omits it gives its consumer no answer — the consumer then refuses
 rather than guessing, so a `pointCount`/dense-length read degrades visibly instead
 of reporting one axis's cardinality for another's.

DependencyRequirement.description:
ONE `run.dependencies[]` entry — a declared library + the version range this entry is
 supported against (#80).

 `deny_unknown_fields` for the reason every other manifest sub-struct here carries it:
 the FIELD SET IS THE CONTRACT. A misspelled `libary:` / `versions:` must be a parse
 error naming the key, not a requirement that silently declares nothing — a dependency
 contract that quietly parses to empty is worse than no contract, because it reports
 the same green build while enforcing nothing.

library.description:
The DISTRIBUTION name as the environment's package index knows it — the name the
 recipe installs and the name the resolved version is looked up by at run time.

 Deliberately the distribution name and NOT the import name: they differ often
 enough that guessing one from the other is a bug source, and the distribution name
 is the one both the recipe's pin set and the run-time metadata lookup are keyed on.
 The recipe's own pin file carries the import name alongside each pin, for the build
 smoke line that is the other consumer.

optional.description:
This entry uses the library only on SOME paths — typically when a parameter
 enables the behaviour that needs it.

 It changes exactly one thing, at run time: an ABSENT optional library is recorded
 as absent instead of refusing the run, because the paths that do not use it are
 legitimate and a package handles the absence with its own named refusal on the path
 that does. Everything else is unchanged — the build gate still requires the
 environment to provide it (an environment that cannot support that path at all is
 a build-time fact, not a run-time surprise), and if it IS installed its version is
 range-checked exactly like a required one, because a run that used it is a run
 whose result depends on it.

 Without this the contract could only express "always needed", and declaring a
 conditionally-used library would break the fallback its own refusal message
 recommends: a run that never took that path would fail for a library it never
 touched.

version.description:
The supported version range, as a comma-ANDed specifier set
 (`==` / `!=` / `>=` / `>` / `<=` / `<` over dotted-numeric releases), e.g.
 `">=1.11,<1.12"`.

 The build gate FAILS CLOSED on any grammar outside that subset rather than
 guessing: a specifier it cannot interpret exactly is a build error naming it, so
 the subset the build enforces can never be looser than what the run time — which
 uses the reference implementation — enforces.

 ONE EXCEPTION, since #192: against a recipe that declares `cyto:ecosystem=r`, this
 is read under R `DESCRIPTION` rules, where `-` and `.` are the same separator. That
 is the correct reading for an R declaration and it is confined to R recipes.

DependentAnalyses.description:
**ITEM-50's response — a discriminated union, deliberately not a nullable number.**

 `Option<usize>` generates `count?: number` in this repo's TS, and `count ?? 0` then
 compiles: the cannot-compute state becomes 0 with nothing to stop it. The consumer is a
 DESTRUCTIVE-ACTION confirmation — stage 3's detach warning — where "0 dependent analyses"
 reads as a safety clearance in front of a user about to remove a dataset three analyses
 depend on.

 So the absence is a VARIANT rather than a missing field. A client must branch on `kind`
 before it can reach a number, which is the same "make the wrong thing inexpressible"
 move the plan asks for elsewhere ("put the recursion in the TYPE, not in prose").

DependentCount.description:
**ITEM-50 — how many analyses in this project used this dataset.**

 **A DISCRIMINATED UNION, and a nullable count was rejected — this comment used to
 describe the rejected design.**

 There are two distinct answers and `0` is only one of them: `Counted { count: 0 }` says
 *"this project's recorded runs used other datasets"*, while `CannotCompute` says *"this
 project has no recorded runs, so a count here would be 0 for a reason that has nothing to
 do with this dataset"*. A client must branch on `kind` before it can reach a number.

 The consumer is a **destructive-action confirmation** (stage 3's detach warning), which is
 the worst place in the round to blur them: *"0 dependent analyses"* on a dialog that
 removes something reads as a safety clearance.

 **Why not `Option<usize>`:** it generates `count?: number`, and `count ?? 0` then
 COMPILES — the cannot-compute state silently becomes zero at the call site, in front of a
 user about to detach a dataset three analyses depend on. Preserving the null "all the way
 to the generated TS" made the absence *visible*, not *unignorable*, and only the second
 one is a guarantee. As a union the collapse does not typecheck, which stage 3's ITEM-39
 confirmed against the live route.

 It is recorded this way rather than simply corrected because the stale version survived
 beside the union it was replaced by, and **prose is what a reader reaches for first** —
 on this branch a doc-comment that outlived its design has been the false premise four
 times, twice in a producer's own docstrings.

oneOf.description: A real count. `0` here means "this project's recorded runs used other datasets".

**Not a number.** The project has no recorded runs, so every count would be 0 for a
 reason that has nothing to do with this dataset.
