 its row was GC'd). The FE renders `v3←v2←v1` + the per-version membership delta from it.

DraftListQuery.description: Query params for the drafts list (`?project_id&kind`).

kind.description: Optional opaque `kind` filter (absent → every kind in the project).

DraftableSpec.description:
The `draftable` block on a `contributes.analyses[]` entry (draftable-entity
 ITEM-9). Every field is an OPAQUE, package-owned string the core carries but never
 interprets (INV-1): `kind` labels the draft's `drafts.kind`; `freeze` names the
 producer analysis id run at freeze; `edit` names the edit view; `freeze_on`
 enumerates the consuming analysis ids that auto-freeze on consumption (ITEM-8).

freeze.description: The producer analysis id run at freeze (its outputs become the frozen artifact).

freeze_on.description: Consuming analysis ids that trigger auto-freeze-on-consume (ITEM-8 / INV-4).

kind.description: The opaque `kind` a draft of this analysis carries (`drafts.kind`).

EligibilityRequest.description:
The eligibility request body — a tagged union carrying exactly one of the two
 request kinds (`{"preview": …}` or `{"inventory": …}`).

EligibilityResponse.description: The eligibility response — per-method verdicts plus the screen-B totals.

total_no_env.description:
The `cannot_run` methods whose reason is
 [`ReasonCode::EnvImageMissing`] — the count of catalogue methods the
 app cannot actually start (no published environment on this
 computer), so the list header can say how many exist while still
 listing them.

EligibilityStatus.description:
The three-method eligibility verdict vocabulary (the board's "Can run / Can
 run for some patients / Cannot run").

EnvIndexStatus.description:
`GET /api/sandbox/envs` (PROV-SS-5): the stack half + the two env indexes.

 The `base`/`layers` split is THIS route's classification job — an
 [`EnvKind::Unknown`] record belongs to neither list (DRIFT-1 #15: the
 manager never guesses base/layer, so an unknown entry only answers the
 per-env `status` route).

oneOf.description:
A trimmed per-language base rootfs
 (`ghcr.io/tinnlab/txresbench-env/…`).
A per-method layer image (`ghcr.io/tinnlab/txr-method-env-layers/…`).

The env has never been ensured in this process and is not persisted, so
 the manager cannot know whether it is a base or a layer. This node is
 deliberately catalogue-free (it never enumerates env names); the caller
 of [`MethodEnvManager::status`] knows the kind from its own records.
 A `Unknown` record is never mounted — `ensure` refuses it.

EnvRef.description:
Reference to one sandboxed artifact (base rootfs or method layer).

 `digest` is the 64-hex sha256 of the artifact's single squashfs layer, taken
 from the caller's catalogue record — verification is always against THIS
 value, never against a moving tag (DEC-3).

digest.description:
The pinned 64-hex sha256 of the squashfs layer the bytes are verified
 against.

oci_ref.description:
Full OCI reference, e.g. `<prefix>/<env_id>[:<tag>][@sha256:<hex>]`
 (prefixes from [`TXR_BASE_REGISTRY_PREFIX`] /
 [`TXR_LAYER_REGISTRY_PREFIX`]; enforced by [`validate_oci_ref`]).

tag.description: Optional tag; resolved only when the reference carries no `@digest`.

EstimateRequest.description:
The estimate request: which methods, on how many patients, on how many
 CPUs, running `at_a_time` lanes.

cpus.description:
The CPU count an estimate is scaled to. Absent (or `null`) means the
 run's own resolution — the host's detected CPUs ([`estimate::host_cpus`],
 the ONE implementation the execution engine's run-start detection also
 calls), so the bar and the running header always employ the same count.
 A present value is used as posted (0 is rejected).

EstimateResponse.description:
The estimate response: per-method seconds, the plain sum, and the
 longest-processing-time schedule total over the `at_a_time` lanes (the
 bottom-bar "about X minutes in total on this computer"). `cpus` is the
 count actually used (the posted value, or the run's own resolution —
 [`estimate::host_cpus`] — when omitted), so the consumer can show the
 number the estimate was scaled to.

target.description: The target run/artifact to walk back from (null = whole project).

ExportTarget.description:
The one-off export record of a save (PROV-MS-3's `also_export` arm) — the
 file is already written; `dir` is where the user's "Open the folder" points.

ExtensionManifest.description:
One extension = one `manifest.yaml` folder. The registry holds one of these per
 discovered `extensions/<id>/manifest.yaml`.

apiVersion.description: The manifest-schema version this extension targets.

contributes.description: The contribution kinds (converters / views / datatypes) this extension adds.

id.description: Stable extension id — the package's own directory name under `packages/`.

FeatureFlagView.description:
One flag as presented on the admin surface: the compiled registry facts plus the
 current global/per-account rows and the RESOLVED effective value for the queried
 account (or the global effective value when no account was queried).

account_enabled.description:
The per-account override's value for the queried account, if one exists (and
 only when an `account_id` was queried). `null` otherwise.

default_enabled.description: The compiled default (the value when no DB row overrides it).

effective.description:
The resolved value: per-account override → global → compiled default. When an
 `account_id` was queried this is that account's effective value; otherwise it
 is the global effective value.

global_enabled.description:
The GLOBAL row's value, if a global row exists (else `null` → the compiled
 default applies globally).

FeaturesListQuery.description:
Optional `?account_id=` for the flag list — resolve the effective/per-account
 columns for this account instead of the global view.

account_id.description:
The account the `effective`/`account_enabled` columns were resolved for
 (`?account_id=`), or `null` for the global view.

File.description:
File entity — the **head view** of a versioned file. The per-version columns
 (`file_size`, `mime_type`, …) reflect the current head version: `files`
 keeps them as a denormalized mirror that `append_version`/`restore_version`
 update in lock-step, so every existing reader of `files.*` transparently
 sees the latest version.

blob_version_id.description:
Storage key for the head version's bytes — equals `current_version_id`
 for a normal head, or the restored target for a restored head. Internal
 resolution detail (callers load blobs by this id).

FileColumns.description: The column-resolution report of one file (PROV-FV-2's `columns`).

covariate_columns.description:
The covariate columns with their numeric-ness (the model's covariate
 input fact: a non-numeric covariate column is not usable as one).

resolved.description:
role wire-key (`patient_id`, `pfs_days`, … `covariate:<name>`) →
 column name, for every column that matched a rule alias (DEC-5).

unresolved.description: Columns known to no rule — reported, never rejected (DEC-5).

FileInspection.description:
The inspect response (PROV-FV-2). The problems cover the per-file checks
 (types, nullability, uniqueness, cross-table references that are
 resolvable single-file, header and required-column problems); the full
 cross-table + join + units + outcome set is the `validate` response's.

FileInspectionRequest.description:
The inspect request body: ONE file, no cross-file context (screen C inspects
 each file as it is dropped; screen N inspects its only file — INV-3).

FileLayout.description:
How an artifact's bytes map to physical files. P1's store already resolves the
 physical members (`is_multifile` + merkle `content_hash`); P2 only DECLARES the
 shape so the reader knows how to assemble (ITEM-14).

oneOf.description: One physical blob.
A prefix of member blobs under one key (a Zarr chunk-dir).

A manifest that maps member-path → member-blob (a data file beside its sidecar
 index; an N-part export whose members are one logical artifact).

FileOutcomes.description:
The file's outcome-column facts — the availability of the four outcome
 column kinds the validator resolves (`responder`/`response_day` for the
 response task, `pfs_*`/`os_*` event + time for the survival task). The
 engine needs them to emit the three outcome-availability verdicts
 (`RESPONSE_LABEL_MISSING`, `SURVIVAL_OUTCOME_MISSING`,
 `TASK_INCOMPATIBLE` — PROV-MC-5's grown vocabulary); they are facts the
 validator knows and puts on the inventory it posts.

has_event.description: The file carries a survival event column (`pfs_event`/`os_event`).

has_responder.description: The file carries a `responder` column (per patient).

has_response_day.description: The file carries a `response_day` column (per patient).

has_survival_day.description: The file carries a survival time column (`pfs_days`/`os_days`).

FileProblem.description:
One reported problem (INV-2: every problem carries its FILE row — 1-based,
 header included — or `null` for file-level; columns are named when the
 problem is a column's, `null` otherwise).

FileSummary.description:
The file-level summary facts of an inspect call (row count, marker columns
 and their row counts, the distinct draw days).

FileTableKind.description:
The two user-file tables (screen C and screen N) — one parsed shape, both
 screens, one validation pipeline (INV-3).

FileVersion.description: One immutable version of a file.

blob_version_id.description: Storage key for this version's bytes (= `id`, or the restored target).

source_message_id.description: The chat turn / tool-call that produced this version (provenance).

ForwardGraphDto.description:
Forward lineage from a dataset (ITEM-21 / DEC-20): every run + output derived
 from THIS dataset until the end (across promote boundaries + fan-out branches).

content_hash.description: The dataset's merkle content hash (the link key); empty if untyped/unhashed.

dataset_id.description: The dataset the forward walk started from.

outputs.description: The artifacts/intermediates produced by those runs.

runs.description: The runs derived from the dataset (topology-agnostic set).

FreezeResponse.description:
The `POST /drafts/{id}/freeze` response (DEC-2 final). The freeze producer runs
 asynchronously as a background job, so the freeze is ACCEPTED (202) with the current
 (still-open) `draft` + the `freeze_job_id` the client can poll; the draft flips to
 `frozen` when that job completes (refetch on the `Draft/Update` sync, or poll). For an
 already-frozen unchanged draft it returns 200 with `freeze_job_id: null` (INV-5
 idempotent — no new job).

freeze_job_id.description: The enqueued freeze producer job to poll (null when the draft was already frozen).

FrontendActionEntry.description:
One frontend action. Field names match CONTRACT.md's `frontend-actions.json`
 schema exactly — the SAME shape whether the entry came from the committed
 app-owned manifest or was REPORTED by the controlled browser session
 (`modules/mcp/capabilities.rs`), so `handlers.rs` has ONE code path.

 This is ALSO the wire shape a session reports (`AgentCapabilitiesBody`). One
 shape, one type: a parallel wire struct would be a second definition of the
 same thing, which is the defect class this module's history is made of. What
 the wire direction adds is not a type but a GATE — the report is untrusted
 input, filtered and bounded by `capabilities::sanitize` before it can reach
 the catalog.

context.description:
Which app CONTEXT (active page/surface) must be live for this action to
 be invokable — `"global"` (always available) or a named context such as
 `"workbench"`/`"dataset"` (workbench-analysis PLAN.md ITEM-4). Surfaced
 by `describe_capability` as a precondition so the AI navigates there
 first; the ENGINE enforces the `CONTEXT_INACTIVE` reject and the backend
 merely RELAYS it (this catalog only carries the value through — the exact
 Layer 5/6 split the `stateful` field follows for staleness).
 `#[serde(default = "default_context")]` keeps a manifest predating this
 field parseable, defaulting to `"global"` — the same back-compat the
 `stateful` field's `#[serde(default)]` provides.

group.description:
Discoverability metadata (richer-actions ITEM-4) — the display GROUP, a
 one-line DESCRIPTION, and ALTERNATIVE search terms (aliases/keywords) the
 frontend `defineAction` carries. Surfaced to the agent by
 `list_capabilities` (searched) + `describe_capability` (shown) so it can
 find/pick an action by intent, not only its exact title. Each
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps a manifest predating these fields parseable
 (the `stateful`/`context` back-compat precedent).

kind.description:
`"global"` (invoked directly by id) or `"instance"` (addresses a
 runtime `view_id` — ai-actions slice 3, ARCHITECTURE.md Layer 4).
 Branched on in `handlers.rs`'s `invoke_frontend`/`describe_capability`
 to thread `view_id`/`expected_token` through to the agent channel.

stateful.description:
Only meaningful when `kind == "instance"`. `true` together with
 `mutating` means invoking this action requires a valid `expected`
 state token (the read-before-write / stale-state guard,
 ARCHITECTURE.md Layer 6) — engine-enforced, this catalog only carries
 the flag through to `describe_capability` + the invoke path.
 `#[serde(default)]` keeps a manifest predating this field parseable.

GraphDto.description: The provenance graph for a project (or a target's backward closure).

HostResourceRequirement.description:
A named, operator-supplied host resource an entry needs mounted read-only (S7).

 The NAME is a deployment contract, not a concept the server understands: an
 operator points `CYTO_SANDBOX_RESOURCE_<NAME>` at a host path and allowlists its
 root via `CYTO_SANDBOX_REFERENCE_MOUNTS`. Nothing about WHAT the resource is — a
 reference index, a model, a lookup table — is encoded here; only "this entry needs
 the resource called X at path Y".

mount_path.description:
The ABSOLUTE in-sandbox path the resource is bound read-only at, e.g.
 `/refdata`. Declared by the package because the ENTRY is what reads it.

name.description:
The resource name the deployment configures, e.g. `reference`. Lowercase
 letters, digits, `_` and `-`; uppercased with `-`→`_` to form the env var.

ImportOutcome.description:
`POST /api/txr/models/import` (201) — the restored rows + the set they were
 imported into. `set_id` is null when the multipart carried no `set_id`
 form field (the container's recorded set is then recreated fresh); the
 reader's default-set rule lives in `store.rs`.

IngestSpec.description:
How an uploaded file becomes an artifact of this type (ITEM-13/16). Drives the
 sniffer's ext/magic ordering.

extensions.description: File extensions (without the dot) that hint this type, e.g. `["csv","tsv"]`.

magic_hex.description: Leading magic-byte signatures as lowercase hex, e.g. `["504b0304"]` (Zarr/zip).

InputRequirements.description:
What file SHAPE an uploaded input of this type must arrive as (ITEM-13). Drives the
 upload wizard's picker + pre-upload validation ("this type needs 3 files or a zip"),
 and supersedes the implicit multi-file auto-grouper — which inferred one specific
 format's trio by filename — with explicit declared intent (DEC-9).

 Shape note: an ARCHIVE is not a distinct requirement — it is the same named
 `members` delivered bundled, so `Manifest { allow_archive: true }` models "the N
 files OR a single `.zip`/`.tar` that expands to them" without a redundant `Archive`
 variant that would duplicate `members`.

oneOf.description: Exactly one file (e.g. a `.csv`).

N named required members that JOINTLY form one dataset — a format whose one
 dataset is several files, the way a shapefile is `.shp` + `.shx` + `.dbf`.
 When `allow_archive` is set, a single `.zip`/`.tar` that expands to those
 members is also accepted.

allow_archive.description: Also accept a single `.zip`/`.tar` archive expanding to `members`.

InventoryCovariate.description: One covariate column of the file inventory.

key.description: The file column key (the validator's stable key).

InventoryEligibilityRequest.description:
The file-inventory body (screens C/N/E — the consumer that holds the file
 posts it).

outcomes.description:
The outcome-column facts of the file, when the consumer knows them
 (absence skips the outcome-availability checks — a request without them
 is not misclassified by the engine).

InventoryMarker.description: One marker column of the file inventory.

has_detection_companion.description:
The column has a `__detected`/`__lod` companion (data.py's companion
 semantics — companions never rank or match).

is_detection_call.description: The column is a detection call (present/absent, not a measured value).

key.description: The file column key (the validator's stable key).

per_patient.description:
Per-patient draw counts; OMITTED when the validator does not carry them
 (coverage then falls back to the patient-level counts above).

InvitationSummary.description:
One row of `GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` — the inviter's view of their
 OWN account's pending invitations.

 **What is deliberately ABSENT is the specification, not an oversight.** There is no
 `user_id`, no `username`, no `display_name`, no `registered` flag and no token or
 hash. Issue #145: *"The list response must never reveal whether a pending invitee is a
 registered user — return the email as typed, `role`, `created_at`, `expires_at`,
 `invited_by`, and nothing user-shaped."* The SQL behind it never joins `users`, so the
 property holds by construction rather than by a projection someone must remember to
 keep narrow.

 **There is no invite LINK here either**, and that follows from the token being hashed
 at rest: the server cannot reproduce a link it has already handed out. The link is
 minted afresh by `POST …/invitations/{id}/resend` (#145 DEC-2).

email.description: The normalized address the invitation was issued to.

invited_by.description:
The inviter's user id — an audit field, not a live reference (the column has no
 FK, so this may name a user who has since been deleted).

InvitationsListResponse.description:
`GET /api/accounts/{account_id}/invitations` response — paged (the settings-list
 numbered-pagination idiom; `total` drives "Showing N of M").

pid.description:
OS pid of the running child (null unless running). Internal-ish but
 harmless for the owner's own job.

req_cpu.description: Requested CPU cores (null = the class default; clamped to the admin ceiling).

req_mem_bytes.description: Requested memory bytes (null = the class default; clamped to the ceiling).

run_id.description:
Provenance run id (P4 owns the semantics).

 NOTE (ITEM-68): a job carries NO scope column. Its tenancy scope (a project
 OR a dataset) lives in the single-source-of-truth `job_scope` table — read
 via [`super::repository::JobRepository::job_scope`]. `jobs` is scope-agnostic.

JobDetail.description:
Job detail: the job plus its captured logs + metric series (for the drawer
 detail view / reload).

can_stop.description:
Same fact as [`JobListItem::can_stop`], on the detail wire — so a surface
 that opened a job directly (a deep link, a reload) renders its Stop control
 from the same server-stated answer the list uses, not from a guess.

milestones.description:
The end-user-facing milestone timeline (ITEM-24), oldest first — so a
 reload / reconnect replays the step ticker, not just the live stream.

JobListItem.description:
One row of the job list: the job, plus the caller-relative facts a client needs
 to render it. Shaped after `DatasetListItem` (`dataset` + its derived
 processing fields), which is this codebase's established way to hand a client a
 row together with what the SERVER says about it for THIS caller.

 [`Self::can_stop`] exists because `11e622bf` made sight and stop-authority
 genuinely different: a third-party editor may list a job and gets **403** on
 `POST /jobs/{id}/stop`. A client that rendered Stop for every active row was
 therefore offering a refusal the user could not have predicted — and the fix is
 NOT for the client to re-derive "creator or scope owner", because that is a
 SECOND copy of an authorization rule, which is the defect this sweep has now
 found six times. The server answers the question; the client renders the answer.

can_stop.description:
Whether THIS caller may stop THIS job — the creator, the owner of the
 dataset/project it is scoped to, or an admin. Read it; do not re-derive it.
 It says nothing about whether the job is still RUNNING: a client still has
 to check `status`, because stopping a finished job is a 409, not a 403.

JobListResponse.description: Paginated job list (mirrors the user module's list response).

JobLogPage.description:
A bounded page of a job's captured log lines (ITEM-12b — long-job scrollback).
 `next_cursor` is the `seq` to pass back as `?after_seq=` for the next forward
 page (null = the end of the log as of this read); `total` is the full line
 count so a client knows the page is a WINDOW, never a silent truncation.

JobLogsQuery.description:
Cursor query for the paged log endpoint. `after_seq` is the stable cursor
 (`seq` is a per-job monotonic key); `limit` is the page size.

after_seq.description:
Return log lines whose `seq` is strictly greater than this cursor
 (0/absent = from the start). Pass back the response's `next_cursor`.

mem_peak_bytes.description:
Whole-cgroup-subtree peak memory (bytes) if a cgroup scope was present
 (ITEM-25); null on the single-pid `ProcSampler` fallback.

pids_current.description: Current process count in the cgroup subtree (null on the sysinfo fallback).

JobMilestone.description:
A recorded end-user-facing milestone transition (`job_milestones`, ITEM-24 /
 DEC-25) — the DECLARED, PERSISTED step timeline the person who LAUNCHED the run
 reads while it runs, distinct from raw `job_logs` (for whoever debugs the run)
 and from the fine progress %. Mirrors [`JobLog`]. `detail` carries the
 structured, data-determined finding the script emitted (e.g. `{rows, columns}`,
 `{count, names}`); persisting it fixes "progress lost on reconnect" and yields a
 provenance-friendly step timeline.

detail.description: The structured finding payload the script emitted (defaults to `{}`).

dispatch_tick_ms.description:
Dispatch (claim) loop cadence, milliseconds (#56). Default 500 == the inline
 `interval(Duration::from_millis(500))` it replaces.

heartbeat_secs.description:
Worker heartbeat cadence, seconds (#56). Read at each scheduler-loop
 iteration; default 10 == `ReaperLimits::default().heartbeat`.

max_reclaims.description:
Poison-job discard-at-max: a row reclaimed this many times is failed, not
 re-queued (#56). Default 5 == `ReaperLimits::default().max_reclaims`.

metric_tick_secs.description:
CPU/RSS metric sampling cadence, seconds (#56). Read once per job execution;
 default 1 == the inline `interval(Duration::from_secs(1))` it replaces.

per_tenant_max_concurrent.description:
T4 (§6 `$per_tenant_cap`): the max jobs ONE owner may have `running` at
 once, folded into the multi-worker-safe claim UPDATE. Distinct from the
 GLOBAL `max_concurrent_jobs` (both are enforced inside the claim, DEC-1).

reaper_tick_secs.description:
Reaper single-leader sweep cadence, seconds (#56). Default 15 ==
 `ReaperLimits::default().reaper_tick`.

reclaim_batch.description:
Bounded reclaim/discard batch per sweep (#56). Default 100 ==
 `ReaperLimits::default().reclaim_batch`.

reserved_interactive_slots.description:
Interactive slots held in reserve so a batch burst never head-of-line-
 blocks a just-arrived interactive re-run (soft admission, DEC-B).

sse_keep_alive_secs.description:
SSE keep-alive/heartbeat interval, seconds (#54). Read at each
 `GET /jobs/{id}/stream` connect; default 15 == the axum `KeepAlive::default()`.

sse_max_clients.description:
Global cap on concurrent per-job SSE subscribers (#54, OOM guard). Read at
 each stream connect; default 256 == `runtime::MAX_SSE_CLIENTS`.

stale_threshold_secs.description:
Stale-reclaim threshold, seconds (#56): a `running` row whose heartbeat is
 older than this is reclaimed as dead. Default 45 == `ReaperLimits::default()
 .stale_threshold`. Bounded `>= 3 * heartbeat_secs` so a live worker is never
 reclaimed (INV-4 / DEC-3).

updated_by.description:
Audit: the acting admin who last PUT these settings (#54; mirrors billing
 INV-4). Stamped server-side from the caller, never from the wire body; null
 until the first PUT.

JobStatusFrame.description: A status-transition frame (the stream's terminal signal too).

JobsListQuery.description: Pagination + scope query for the job list.

project_id.description:
Filter to jobs scoped to this project (ITEM-67 project jobs panel) via the
 `job_scope` JOIN. Absent → all of the caller's (or, for an admin, everyone's)
 jobs regardless of scope.

JoinOffer.description:
A join offer the user accepted: every `variants` spelling of one logical
 marker column merges into the single `key` (DEC-12: nothing is ever
 auto-applied — an `A03` problem is a QUESTION; the user's `joins[]` entry
 is the answer).

LayoutKind.description:
The domain-neutral storage layout a datatype's artifacts use. Keyed on LAYOUT,
 never on domain (DEC-4) — every layout below is one option among several and NONE
 is privileged, so no domain's favourite physical shape becomes the core's default.
 Maps to P1's coarse `workstore::artifact::StorageLayout` string via
 [`LayoutKind::as_storage_layout`].

oneOf.description: A chunked dense array (Zarr) — e.g. a low-dimensional coordinate array.
A chunked sparse array (CSC/CSR) — e.g. a large sparse measurement matrix.

A columnar table (Parquet) — e.g. a per-row statistics table / label
 codes+categories.

A chunked 1-D vector — e.g. a metadata column / genomic track. The explicit
 `rename` is REQUIRED: serde's `snake_case` renders `Chunked1d` as `chunked1d`
 (no underscore around a digit), which would diverge from the TS mirror's
 `chunked_1d` and the `chunked-1d` DB string. Pin it.
An opaque blob served as-is (no host decode) — e.g. an HTML report.

password.description:
User's existing local password — the auth proof for binding
 the social identity.

ListVersionsQuery.description:
Optional pagination for the versions list. Defaults bound an
 un-paginated caller to the most recent `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` versions
 (newest first) instead of returning an unbounded set.

ListedArtifact.description:
A catalog list-row: the artifact PLUS the two DERIVED provenance facts a consumer
 cannot reconstruct from the row itself — WHICH DATASET it came from (ITEM-22) and
 WHAT PRODUCED it. The picker groups/labels candidates by the first, so a user with
 several datasets attached to a project can tell the analysis inputs apart.
 Both are DERIVED from provenance — NOT denormalized columns (ITEM-21).
 `Artifact` is flattened (mirrors `dataset::DatasetListItem`) so the wire shape is a
 plain `Artifact` + these extra fields; existing readers see the same fields.

dataset_id.description:
Dataset (owner) tenancy scope (the datasets-management processing path).
 NULL for a project-scoped artifact. Exactly one of `project_id`/`dataset_id`
 is set on a live artifact (ITEM-23).

datatype.description: Opaque to the host; validated against P2's registry.

generator_id.description:
**WHO PRODUCED THIS ARTIFACT** — the ANALYSIS id recorded by the producing run
 (`provenance_run_repro.generator_id`, joined on the row's own `run_id`), which is
 the same id an analysis contributes under (`contributes.analyses[].id`).

 The row already carries `run_id`, and a run id alone answers "which execution"
 but never "which analysis" — so a consumer asking whether a column is ITS OWN
 previous output had nothing to compare against, and every producer looked alike.
 That is the whole reason this field exists: a form whose emitted column names are
 its own defaults must be able to tell "I made this last time" from "something
 else made this", and the difference decides whether a re-run is refused.

 NULL when the artifact names no producing run (an import / upload / seeded row),
 or when the producing run recorded no provenance — both are "not attributable",
 and a consumer must read them as such rather than as any particular producer.
 DERIVED, like the two fields above: it is a join, never a column on `artifacts`.

hidden.description:
Excluded from catalog/picker LISTINGS (still fetchable by id) — set on
 derived alternate-representation artifacts (ITEM-20).

is_multifile.description: Whether `object_key` points at a manifest (members resolved through it).

logical_bytes.description:
The size the data REPRESENTS when materialised — the number a user reads as
 "Size", and the only one that belongs in a byte total on screen. Equals
 `stored_bytes` for an artifact that owns a blob; `rows × element width` for a
 gathered one.

 `None` means genuinely UNKNOWN, not zero. It is an `Option` so that every
 consumer — and, through the generated TypeScript, every UI consumer — has to
 decide what to show when there is no answer. Rendering `0 Bytes` for a
 500,000-row gathered column is the defect this type prevents.

meta.description: Producer-declared: what the artifact means, for display. Same contract.

object_key.description:
The data blob key (single-file) or the manifest blob key (multi-file) —
 or `None` when this artifact has NO STORED BYTES (ITEM-16).

 `None` is not "unknown" and not "empty": it means the row is GATHERED, and
 `structure.gathered_from` carries the recipe that produces the bytes on
 demand. The `artifacts_bytes_or_recipe` CHECK constraint enforces that
 exactly one of the two is present, so a reader may treat `None` as a
 GUARANTEE that the recipe is there rather than as a case to guess about.

 Every consumer of this field must decide what a gathered artifact means for
 it. There is deliberately no `unwrap_or_default()` anywhere: an empty object
 key is a valid-looking address that resolves to nothing, which is the
 antipattern `202608040002_artifact_model_drop.sql` removed from four other
 columns. Sites that cannot yet serve a gathered artifact return a named
 refusal citing the ITEM that owes the real behaviour.

project_id.description:
Project tenancy scope (the P11 workbench path). NULL for a dataset-scoped
 artifact (ITEM-23): an artifact is scoped to a project OR a dataset (owner).

representation_of.description:
The source artifact this row is an alternate encoding of (ITEM-20); NULL
 for a first-class artifact.

role.description:
Producer-declared TIER (DEC-8): `artifact` = promotable/exportable,
 `intermediate` = viz-only. A first-class column for the same reason `hidden`
 is one — it is a property the SERVER acts on (the promote gate), not display
 data. It is deliberately NOT re-derived from `meta`: `meta` is the producer's
 declaration carried verbatim, and reading operational meaning out of it would
 restate in another column exactly what dropping `params` (ITEM-7) removed.
 Never empty, and NOT because a blank is normalized here: a blank or omitted
 `role` is REFUSED upstream by `sandbox::outputs::deserialize_declared_role`,
 and this struct carries no `#[serde(default)]`. The former `role_or_default`
 mapped blank → `artifact` — blank ⇒ the PROMOTABLE tier — and was deleted
 rather than fixed, so absence cannot resolve to a privilege (INV-2).

run_id.description: The producing run; null for source/upload artifacts.

source_dataset_id.description:
The dataset this artifact derives from — **only when there is exactly one**.

 NULL means "not one dataset", which is TWO different situations the field deliberately
 does not distinguish: no source at all, or SEVERAL. Both are cases where a consumer
 scoping something to a single dataset has no honest answer, and that is the whole point.
 It previously reported the FIRST-DECLARED source of a multi-source artifact, so an
 integration of Dataset 1 + Dataset 2 read as "Dataset 1" — a confident wrong answer
 decided by edge declaration order. A consumer that wants to say something about a
 multi-source artifact reads {@link source_dataset_ids} and states its own disposition.

source_dataset_ids.description:
EVERY dataset this artifact derives from (a provenance walk), in declared-input
 order, deduped. Empty when the lineage resolves to no dataset (a bare project-scoped
 seed/output). An artifact produced by INTEGRATING two datasets has two entries.

 This is the authoritative field; the two singular ones below are a convenience that
 only speaks when there is nothing to be ambiguous about.

source_dataset_name.description:
The single source dataset's display NAME, under the same exactly-one rule as
 {@link source_dataset_id}; NULL when there is not exactly one, or when that one
 dataset has since been deleted.

source_dataset_names.description:
The display NAMES matching {@link source_dataset_ids}, same order. An id whose dataset
 has since been deleted contributes no name, so this can be SHORTER than the id list —
 pair them by looking a name up, never by index.

status.description:
`pending|ready|failed`. `failed` is also what the post-ingest conformance
 gate (ITEM-18 / DEC-12) writes when an artifact's bytes disagree with its
 declared `structure`.

stored_bytes.description:
Bytes written to the OBJECT STORE — 0 for a gathered artifact, which owns no
 blob, and that 0 is the correct storage answer. The only reader that wants this
 is the provenance export (its size cap and `fetch.txt`). It is emphatically NOT
 a display size: see [`Self::logical_bytes`].

structure.description:
Producer-declared: how to decode the bytes. The server stores and serves
 this; it never interprets it. No default — an artifact whose producer
 declared no structure is an error at ingest, not an empty object.

LocalSession.description:
The minted session for the single local owner, shape-compatible with the
 desktop `auto_login` command's return.

provider.description:
Optional provider name for LDAP/OAuth authentication
 If not specified, defaults to local password authentication

One resolved marker column of the file (after joins and mappings) — the
 per-marker facts the C/N card renders and the inventory is built from.

Every spelling that merged into this key (`["ldh", "LDH"]` after a
 join — EXAMPLE-FV-1).

The per-marker coverage counts (EXAMPLE-FV-3: the board's "needs 3 or more

MarkerFacts.description:
The marker-input facts recorded on a saved model at save time (the
 catalogue's [`MarkerKind`]/[`UsesHistory`] vocabulary verbatim — a model
 INSTANCE's facts, since the D5-selected feature set is per instance).

The marker-input shape of a method: `any` (marker-agnostic; `count` 0 =

How many runnable methods reference this marker (the join-offer
 weight — a marker 300 methods rank differently from one 3 do).

The raw registry system spelling (`LOINC`, `HGNC`, … — the open-string
 system, same as `StandardId.system`, never a closed list here).

MarkerSummary.description: One marker column's inspect summary (name → value-row count).

MarkerSystem.description:
The marker identifier system of a vocabulary marker (the registry's systems;
 the matching engine also knows the `other`-system fallback as an open string).

MarkerVocabularyResponse.description:
The marker-vocabulary response (the join-offer + the B-screen group-panel
 vocabulary; the checkbox set is built from `groups`).

MatchKind.description:
The matched item kind (DEC-12 match ladder: exact display name → alias →
 standard id → fuzzy containment suggestion, in that order; fuzzy is a
 suggestion only).

MatchMode.description: The `required_markers` match mode (the data.py port's `match:` field).

McpSettings.description:
The singleton MCP settings row — the six promoted knobs (agent caps + tool
 caps + pairing-TTL). All fields are `bigint`/`i64` (DEC-5), converted to
 `usize`/`u64`/`Duration` at the read-at-use sites via the accessors below.

action_wall_clock_secs.description:
Outer wall-clock backstop on a single dispatched frontend action, in
 seconds. Source: `agent_channel.rs WALL_CLOCK_CAP` (15 min = 900s).

max_control_sessions.description:
Global cap on live agent control-session connections (OOM guard — SAFETY,
 DEC-3). One session per user, so it effectively caps concurrent AI-paired
 users. Source: `agent_channel.rs MAX_CONTROL_SESSIONS`.

max_inflight_per_user.description:
Per-user cap on concurrent in-flight frontend-action invokes (DoS guard —
 SAFETY, DEC-3). Source: `agent_channel.rs MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_USER`.

max_list_results.description:
Cap on how many capabilities `list_capabilities` returns in one call.
 Source: `handlers.rs MAX_LIST_RESULTS`.

max_result_bytes.description:
Cap on the REST-invoke result body relayed back to the model, in bytes
 (OOM guard — SAFETY, DEC-3). Source: `handlers.rs MAX_RESULT_BYTES` (1 MiB).

pairing_ttl_secs.description:
Pairing-code time-to-live, in seconds. Source: `pairing.rs
 PAIRING_TTL_MINUTES` (5 min = 300s).

has_password.description:
Whether this account has a local password set (`password_hash IS
 NOT NULL`). `password_hash` itself is never serialized, so this
 derived flag is how the client decides whether to offer a
 self-service "change password" form (false for OAuth/LDAP-only).

permissions.description: Effective permissions (union of user's direct permissions + all active group permissions)

MeasurementsSummary.description: The measurements-table summary facts of a validate call.

distinct_draw_days.description:
The distinct draw days, ascending (the "draw times" the engine and the
 screen B schedule need).

patients.description:
Distinct patients in the measurements table (the predict-mode
 cohort — TEST-FV-9).

One method's full fact set — the `methods[]` entry of the committed catalogue

Never fetched (or the persisted state no longer applies — a crash

The verified artifact is cached; `ensure` returns its mount directly.
The last attempt failed (or was cancelled); `error` names the reason.

Whether the artifact's mount is currently live (the cache mount's
 `usr/` is visible, or the staged dir carries it).

MethodGroup.description: The four benchmark method groups (the group chips on the list screen).

oneOf.description: A rule/statistic that calls response vs no response at the decision day.
A model of response probability at the decision day.
A risk score from baseline values.
A landmark / joint / dynamic model of risk over time.

MethodListQuery.description:
The optional list filters. Every field is typed so an unparseable value is
 a framework 400, never a silently-ignored filter (all four are optional —
 their absence is the full list).

group.description:
Filter to one method group (`response-call | response-probability |
 static-risk | dynamic-risk`).

q.description: Case-insensitive substring on the method id.

runnable.description:
Filter to runnable / non-runnable entries. (The shipped catalogue is the
 runnable set — DEC-2 — so this is a contract future for the fixture
 world and for consumers that must reason about both.)

MethodListResponse.description:
The `GET /api/methods` response — the full (unpaged) runnable set, bounded at
 roughly 400 rows; the list screen filters client-side (DEC-11).

MethodRunMode.description:
What one stacked run does (DEC-5). Maps to the container contract's
 mode field (X1): unset = one fit+predict call, `fit` / `predict`. The
 sandbox emits it under BOTH spellings, `SIGBENCH_MODE` (X1-era name) and
 `TXRESBENCH_MODE` (the 2.0 SDK's name — see TEST-05 / DRIFT-1 ITEM-3).

Single call: fit on the bundle, predict the same patients (X1's unset
 mode).

`SIGBENCH_MODE`/`TXRESBENCH_MODE=fit`; the derived `/model` is
 written to `model_out_dir`.

`SIGBENCH_MODE`/`TXRESBENCH_MODE=predict` on an already-trained,
 verified model bound read-only at `/model` (INV-4).

base.description: The trimmed per-language base rootfs (DEC-13: always caller-named).

bundle_dir.description: Host dir of the contract-shaped input bundle (bound RO at `/input`).

Host dir the fit's `/model` is written to (under the staging tree —

Per-run CPU cap: `OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS` are set to this value
 (after the prefix's `1` defaults — last-wins, TEST-05).

outputs_dir.description: Host dir where `/output` is written (under the staging tree — DEC-6).

Optional wall-clock timeout override (seconds); the run seam clamps it
 to the admin cap exactly like `clamp_timeout`.

MethodRunResult.description:
Outcome of one stacked run (PROV-SS-1). `exit_code` etc. mirror the shipped
 `SandboxRunResult`; the digests + model facts are the method-run extras
 (INV-6).

layer_env_digest.description: The method-layer digest recorded in the run workspace.

model_out_digest.description:
`tree_sha256` of the fit's `/model` (a trained-model dir), when a
 `model_out_dir` was given.

model_verified.description: The model digest check ran and passed (`ReuseModel` only).

MethodSummary.description:
The list-row projection — the full PROV-MC-1 fact set minus the
 detail-only fields (description/software/licence/references/params and the
 internal-ish gate/env/fitted/saves_model/own_outputs facts). Named explicitly
 so a consumer binds the exact row vocabulary (the E-row performance text and
 the models-dialog warning bind named fields here).

MethodsNarration.description:
The DECLARATIVE methods narration for one analysis (S3).

 ## Why this exists

 `provenance/export/methods.rs` hardcoded ONE processor's analysis id in a
 `*_GENERATOR_ID` constant, that processor's param vocabulary, its input-slot
 spellings, and that processor's own axis noun in prose at nine sites. Since the
 `kind` of EVERY sandbox compute run is the literal `"compute"`, any OTHER
 processor — and every other deployment — got `"Step 'compute' was performed"`
 forever. methods.md is the OUT-OF-APP trust deliverable, so that is the worst
 place in the tree for a hardcoded processor id.

 The narrator still owns the RENDERING (it must, to keep the "never silently drop
 a term" guarantee mechanical); a package declares only the NOUNS and which ROLE
 each of its params plays.

action.description: The past-tense verb: `"<Subjects> were <action> on …"`. e.g. `filtered`.

allow_list_slots.description:
Input SLOT names that carry an explicit element-id allow-list. Such a slot is
 recorded only as a used edge, so a params-only reading cannot see it at all
 and the narration would describe a laxer method than the one that ran.

commits.description:
The noun phrase for what a run COMMITS, appended as `", committing <commits>"`.

 ## Placeholders

 `{label}` is a RESERVED alias for the value of whichever param is declared
 [`MethodsParamRole::OutputLabel`], whatever that param is spelled. Any OTHER
 `{token}` names a PARAM of this analysis directly and is filled from the run's
 recorded value for it.

 Every token must be DECLARED — `label`, or a key of [`Self::params`]. An
 undeclared token is a package-scoped BUILD failure
 (`build_helper::processor_manifest`), never a verbatim render: `{label}` used to
 be the only token substituted, so five shipped manifests spelling `{name}` /
 `{n_pcs}` / `{n_hvg}` / `{method}` printed their braces straight into the
 out-of-app trust deliverable, invisible until a human opened an exported bundle
 (#131).

 A token the RUN did not record is a different case the build cannot see (an
 older run, an unset optional param); the narrator then falls back to
 [`Self::commits_unlabeled`], and omits the clause entirely if that does not
 resolve either. A phrase is only ever emitted once FULLY substituted.

commits_unlabeled.description:
The `commits` phrase to use when the labelled phrase cannot be fully resolved
 (classically: no `output_label` was recorded). Declared separately rather than
 substituting an empty `{label}`, which would emit a half-formed name (an empty
 backticked slot) into the out-of-app trust deliverable.

note.description:
A trailing caveat, narrated UNCONDITIONALLY.

 It used to be appended only when at least one constraint was narrated, so an
 analysis declaring no constraint-producing param role had its ENTIRE scientific
 caveat silently dropped from every exported `methods.md`, with every gate green
 (#131) — five of the six shipped declarations were in that state. The dropped
 text is what a package author writes precisely because the result is easy to
 over-read: the honest parts were the parts being dropped.

params.description:
The ROLE each of this analysis' params plays in the narration. A param NOT
 listed here is disclosed BY NAME rather than dropped, so a knob added
 tomorrow degrades to a named gap and never to an understated method.

reference_assets.description:
The VERSIONED EXTERNAL RESOURCES a run of this analysis consumed — a pretrained
 model, a pinned reference build, a reference-database release, an ontology
 version, a pinned reference artifact (#77).

 ## Why a first-class block and NOT an eighth param role

 A role cannot express a GROUPED tuple: the four facets of one asset would be
 four unrelated role entries with nothing binding them, and two assets would be
 indistinguishable from one. And the nearest EXISTING role,
 [`MethodsParamRole::OpaquePredicate`], renders an actively-WRONG sentence over a
 model — "a recorded `model` expression (not narrated here — see `manifest.json`)"
 — when a pinned model is not a predicate and *is* narratable. Without this
 block the most consequential input to a model-consuming analysis lands in the
 undeclared-param footnote: honest, but a gap statement rather than a narration,
 in the one artefact meant to travel outside the app.

 Empty for every analysis that declares nothing, which is every shipped manifest
 today — so this is purely additive.

subject.description:
The noun for the axis elements this analysis acts on (`row` / `well` /
 `region` / `read`). Prose only — no logic depends on it.

MethodsParamRole.description:
The role a declared param plays in the methods narration (S3). Each names a
 SHAPE the narrator already knows how to render — never a domain.

oneOf.description:
`[{column, control?, min?, max?, keep?}]` — rendered as range / keep-set
 predicate phrases (the same coercion the committed mask used).

A list of `[{metric|col|criteria, min, max, …}]`, where every FURTHER key is a
 qualifier the PROCESSOR itself named and is rendered under that name — OR the
 nested per-group map `{measure: {group: [lo, hi]}}`. Both render in the same
 range grammar (`threshold_phrases`); the role fixes only the measure and bound
 spellings and never a qualifier noun, so no one package's vocabulary reaches
 the out-of-app methods deliverable.

A payload this narrator cannot render faithfully. DISCLOSED by name, with a
 pointer at `manifest.json` — never dropped, never guessed.

An explicit element-id allow-list intersected into the result; its SIZE is
 narrated (the ids themselves are the pinned input, not a parameter).

A cap after which a SEEDED RANDOM subsample runs — the single most
 reproducibility-critical fact a method can have, and the easiest to omit.
The RNG seed.
A user label that names the committed output (fills `commits`' `{label}`).

A SCALAR whose recorded value the narration STATES — interpolated into the
 `commits` phrase by `{<param>}` where the phrase names it, and otherwise stated by
 value in the trailing disclosure. It constrains nothing.

 It exists so a placeholder can be DECLARED and therefore build-checked. Without
 a declared vocabulary the placeholder lint has nothing to check a token against,
 which is "silently accept anything" in a different costume — the exact failure
 being repaired. The shipped case is a phrase interpolating two SIZE parameters:
 neither is a label, so under the narrow `{label}`-only substitution both had no
 home at all and would simply have been deleted from the sentence.

 It does NOT buy the param an exemption from disclosure: a `narrated_value`
 whose phrase was not actually emitted falls BACK into the "Additional recorded
 parameters are NOT narrated here" list, because declared-but-unrendered would
 otherwise be a hole in the never-drop guarantee.

MethodsReferenceAsset.description:
ONE versioned external resource a run consumed (#77).

 Every field except `kind` names a PARAM of the analysis; the narrator reads the
 run's RECORDED value for that param. The declaration is therefore static (it lives
 in the manifest) while the identity and version it narrates are per-run facts —
 which is the whole point: two runs of the same analysis against two model versions
 must narrate differently.

 `name` and `version` are REQUIRED because an asset narrated without its version is
 exactly the untraceability #77 exists to close. `source` and `digest` are optional
 detail. An asset whose `name` or `version` param the run did not record is NOT
 narrated — and its params fall back into the undeclared-param disclosure, so the
 never-drop guarantee holds rather than being quietly satisfied by a half-asset.

digest.description:
The param carrying the asset's CONTENT DIGEST (e.g. `model_sha256`) — the one
 facet that pins the bytes rather than the name.

kind.description:
The package-owned NOUN for what class of resource this is — `pretrained model`,
 `reference database`, `ontology`, `reference build`. Prose only; the core
 carries it and never interprets it (the domain-blindness rule).

name.description: The param carrying the asset's IDENTITY (e.g. `model`).

source.description:
The param carrying where the asset came from (e.g. `model_source`) — a URL, a
 registry id, a release name.

version.description: The param carrying the asset's VERSION (e.g. `model_version`).

MethodsSubject.description: The singular/plural noun for one element of the axis an analysis acts on.

MilestoneFrame.description:
One end-user-facing MILESTONE transition drained from the in-sandbox progress
 FIFO (ITEM-24 / DEC-25): a manifest-declared step `id`, its `status`
 (`started|done|failed`), and an optional structured `detail` payload the script
 emits as it inspects the data (e.g. `{rows, columns}`, `{count: 3, names: […]}`).
 Distinct from the fine `ProgressFrame` %: this is the "what step" checklist the
 person WATCHING the run sees, in the manifest's own declared step vocabulary
 rather than in runtime internals. Surfaced on the job SSE as a `milestone` frame
 and persisted to `job_milestones`.

The inventory list's optional filters (all optional; `q` is a substring on

A saved model dir the reuse run binds READ-ONLY at `/model` after

The `tree_sha256` digest recorded at save time; the run seam recomputes

A model's provenance kind (DEC-16: the user's own `.txr` file needs no

One structured reason of a model verdict (code + per-code params; the

ModelReasonCode.description:
The model eligibility reason-code vocabulary: PROV-MC-5's [`ReasonCode`]
 set (the SAME wire strings — a per-code renderer in the UI never meets an

PackageOrigin.description:
Where a scanned package CAME FROM — the axis the load-failure posture turns on
 (#190/#197).

 A package the compile-time seed manages shipped from `src-app/packages/`: it was linted
 by `build.rs` (with `lint_processor_tree`, the WHOLE-tree validator) before it was
 embedded, so a runtime rejection of it means our build gate and our runtime gate
 DISAGREE about our own artifact. That is a refusal, not a degradation. A package that
 arrived by DROP-IN is untrusted input, and refusing to boot over one would let anyone
 who can write a file under `<data_root>/processors/` brick the server — so it keeps the
 tolerant skip (`mod.rs`'s reflect contract, INV-2).

 **Derived, never enumerated.** The candidate set is
 [`embedded::seed_managed_id_set`], built from the embedded seed itself — there is no
 list for a new package to be forgotten from.

 ## The name is NOT sufficient, and the difference is a denial of service

 A first draft classified purely on the folder NAME. That is wrong, and the way it is
 wrong inverts the whole argument above: `<data_root>/processors/` is writable at
 runtime — D2 runtime drop-in discovery requires exactly that — and the seed reconcile
 no-clobber for CONTENT (`embedded.rs`'s `plan_repair` compares embedded-vs-recorded
 digests and "never reads disk content"). So an attacker who can write one file can
 overwrite a SEED package's `manifest.yaml` with garbage, keep the seed-managed name,
 and — under a name-only rule — earn a permanent, restart-surviving boot refusal. The
 exact denial of service the tolerant drop-in posture exists to avoid, reached through
 the trusted branch.

 So [`Self::of_bytes`] additionally requires the on-disk `manifest.yaml` to be
 BYTE-IDENTICAL to the one this binary embedded, and every other case (edited, replaced,
 symlinked elsewhere, legitimately newer than the embed) falls to the TOLERANT posture.
 The classification is deliberately fail-safe in that direction: any doubt about
 provenance degrades to "that package absent", never to a refusal.

 ## What it verifies, stated exactly

 The MANIFEST, and only the manifest — not `compute/*`, not `ui/*`. That is the right
 scope for the one thing this verdict decides: whether the whole-tree validator
 `build.rs` ran over this manifest and the per-package validator the runtime ran over the
 same bytes DISAGREE. Both validators read the manifest and nothing else, so the manifest
 is exactly the evidence the disagreement is about. It is NOT an integrity claim over the
 package's executable payload: the seed reconcile never reads disk content, so an
 overwritten `compute/*.py` survives every restart while the manifest still matches. Do
 not grow a privilege off this verdict without widening what it checks — the seed
 manifest already records a per-file digest set, which is where that would start.

 It is also the WRONG predicate for deciding which of two colliding packages to protect,
 because an attacker can break byte-equality on OUR package with one appended newline.
 `resolve_cross_package` keys protection on the seed-managed NAME for that reason; see
 its `is_shipped`.

oneOf.description: Shipped in the binary's embedded seed AND still carrying the embedded bytes.

Everything else: a runtime drop-in, or a seed-named folder whose manifest no longer
 matches what was embedded.
